articles.title: Sophie Cunningham could be on her way out of Indiana as the Fever face a major offseason decision
articles.standfirst: The shooting guard will be a free agent after a season in which she stood out off the bench. Stephanie White has already explained what type of players Indiana needs to take the next step.
articles.summary: The shooting guard will be a free agent after a season in which she stood out off the bench. Stephanie White has already explained what type of players Indiana needs to take the next step.
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham’s future with the Indiana Fever is yet to be decided. After their elimination by the Las Vegas Aces in the first round of the WNBA playoffs, the franchise must begin planning for next season with Caitlin Clark and Aliyah Boston as its cornerstones. But there are two issues that require immediate attention: Cunningham and Kelsey Mitchell are both at the end of their contracts and will be unrestricted free agents.

Cunningham was Indiana's leading scorer off the bench in 2026, averaging 7.9 points per game and shooting 41.9% from three-point range in 43 games. Her production dipped during August and September, and she averaged 7.3 points in the series against Las Vegas. General manager Amber Cox valued her leadership and presence in the locker room, although she did not confirm whether the franchise will seek to re-sign her.

Stephanie White explained what Indiana needs

'Coach Stephanie White gave a hint about the direction she wants for the team. In addition to trying to retain Mitchell, she pointed out that the Fever need to find "complementary pieces for our Big 3", made up of Mitchell, Clark, and Boston.'

White described the profile she is looking for: a long, athletic forward, capable of defending the perimeter, pressuring opponents, helping on the boards, attacking the rim, and providing a constant threat from three-point range. She also highlighted the importance of getting more consistent production from the bench.

Cunningham has one of the virtues that fit that idea: outside shooting. In her two seasons with Indiana, she made 42.4% of her three-pointers. However, defense could be a decisive factor in determining her place in the project. The player herself acknowledged that she wants to raise her intensity in that area and establish herself as a 3-and-D specialist, that is, a player who contributes both on defense and in three-point shooting.

About her future, Cunningham avoided making predictions. "I don’t know what the offseason has in store for me", she said on her podcast No Hesitation.

Caitlin Clark also referred to the team’s makeup and pointed to defense as one of the areas Indiana must improve in order to compete more consistently. Her approach aligns with White’s pursuit: a team capable of maintaining its offensive production and responding better on the other side of the court.

Kelsey Mitchell, the Fever's priority

Kelsey Mitchell's situation could affect the rest of the moves. The shooting guard is coming off averaging 24.7 points per game, and the franchise has expressed its desire to keep her long term . However, Mitchell also did not guarantee her continuity and acknowledged that she will have to weigh her own interests before making a decision.

The player also spoke about the emotional toll that constant exposure surrounding the team and having to compete under the scrutiny of the fans can create. Her statements added another dimension to a negotiation that is not limited to the sporting aspect.

Clark, for her part, expressed her desire to keep playing alongside Mitchell and backed her teammate after her comments about the pressure surrounding the Fever. For Indiana, retaining one of its leading scorers appears to be one of the market’s priorities. What happens with Mitchell will also influence planning for the rest of the roster.

When will Sophie Cunningham's future be known?

The exact date of WNBA free agency for 2027 has not yet been officially confirmed. Therefore, there is no specific day to know whether Cunningham will stay in Indiana or listen to offers from other franchises. The negotiation will also depend on how the new Fever roster is resolved and how much room remains to strengthen other positions.

While awaiting that decision, Cunningham already has work scheduled. The American will play in Project B, a new international professional 5-on-5 league set to begin in 2027 and travel through cities in Europe, Asia, and America. The project was co-founded by Grady Burnett, a former Facebook and Google executive, and Geoff Prentice, co-founder of Skype, and will also feature Kelsey Mitchell. Cunningham explained that she plans to play from January to April, just before WNBA training camp. Valencia, from March 12 to 22, and Tokyo, from March 26 to April 4, are already among the confirmed stops of a competition that aims to operate with a traveling Grand Prix format.

“It’s going to be incredible. I’m going to play from January to April, until training camp begins. We’re going to be in several countries,” Cunningham said on October 5. “It will be a great opportunity to expand my brand globally, but at the same time I’ll be able to come back, keep making money, and also enjoy the offseason.”

Cunningham's continuity remains open . Her ability to score from the perimeter and her experience in the locker room work in her favor, but Indiana is looking to improve its defense and first needs to resolve Mitchell's future. Those decisions will determine how much of a place the guard will have in the project the Fever are building around Clark and Boston.

articles.title: Who is favored to win the WNBA finals? Expert picks, predictions and odds for the Golden State Valkyries vs Atlanta Dream series
articles.standfirst: The Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream are preparing to compete for their first WNBA championship, with the 2026 Finals beginning on October 17
articles.summary: The Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream are preparing to compete for their first WNBA championship, with the 2026 Finals beginning on October 17
articles.body:
The 2026 WNBA Finals will feature an unexpected but compelling matchup between the Golden State Valkyries and the Atlanta Dream .

Both teams have eliminated established championship contenders to reach the final, setting up a best-of-seven series with a historic prize at stake.

According to the latest odds published by the WNBA through BetMGM, the Valkyries are slight favorites to win the championship, priced at -115, while Atlanta is listed at -105.

Those numbers indicate a narrow advantage for Golden State rather than a decisive prediction that the series will go its way.

The Finals begin Saturday, October 17, at Chase Center in San Francisco. Golden State earned home-court advantage after finishing the regular season with a 32-12 record, while Atlanta enters the championship round as the fourth seed after a 30-14 campaign.

Both teams have built momentum at exactly the right time, although their paths to the final have been different.

Golden State reached the Finals in only its second season as a WNBA franchise. The Valkyries followed a hard-fought first-round series against Dallas by sweeping the defending champion Las Vegas Aces in the semifinals.

Atlanta, meanwhile, swept Washington before eliminating the New York Liberty in three games, leaving the Dream undefeated in the playoffs.

That contrast makes this matchup particularly intriguing. Golden State has the benefit of home court and a reputation for defensive discipline, while Atlanta has demonstrated that it can handle high-pressure games and produce offense against elite opposition.

Expert predictions: Why Golden State has the edge, but Atlanta cannot be dismissed

The betting market gives Golden State a narrow advantage, and several analysts have also backed the Valkyries to win the series. However, expert predictions are far from unanimous, with some believing Atlanta's offensive depth and recent improvement could be decisive.

In predictions published by The Athletic and republished by Yahoo Sports, Brian Hamilton selected Golden State to win in six games, while Marcus Thompson II backed the Valkyries in seven.

Annie Costabile and Chantel Jennings both predicted an Atlanta victory in seven games, illustrating how closely matched the finalists appear.

Golden State's strongest argument is its defense. The Valkyries limited the Las Vegas Aces during their semifinal sweep and have relied on collective effort, depth and disciplined preparation throughout the postseason.

Gabby Williams has also emerged as a major offensive contributor, giving the team a player capable of making a difference when games become tight.

Atlanta has its own reasons for confidence. Angel Reese has been influential on the boards, while Jordin Canada has supplied scoring and playmaking. Rhyne Howard remains an important perimeter threat, and DeWanna Bonner 's experience gives the Dream another option in crucial moments.

The availability of Allisha Gray could be one of the most important variables. The Atlanta guard injured her left hand during the semifinals and underwent a minor procedure, leaving her status for the start of the Finals uncertain.

If she is unable to play or is limited, the Dream could lose a key part of their scoring attack.

articles.title: Tennis legend Chris Evert calls for a tribute to Caitlin Clark following her controversial remarks
articles.standfirst: Former World No. 1 tennis star believes the WNBA should embrace Caitlin Clark
articles.summary: Former World No. 1 tennis star believes the WNBA should embrace Caitlin Clark
articles.body:
Tennis legend Chris Evert has renewed her support for Caitlin Clark , arguing that the WNBA should celebrate the Indiana Fever star and the attention she’s brought to women’s basketball.

“The WNBA should be celebrating her,” Evert wrote on X, replying to a viral post describing Clark as the most powerful female athlete in the world. The wording wasn’t quite accurate.

In October 2025, Forbes published “America’s Most Powerful Women in Sports.” Clark ranked fourth, behind New Orleans Saints and Pelicans owner Gayle Benson , FanDuel chief executive Amy Howe and Nike executive Amy Montagne.

She was the highest-ranked active athlete on that list, but it covered influential American women in sports rather than naming the world’s most powerful female athlete.

Other sports figures recognized included Napheesa Collier and Breanna Stewart , who were listed together at ninth, tennis great Serena Williams at 11, Coco Gauff at 13 and four-time WNBA MVP A’ja Wilson at 15. Even with the viral claim needing clarification, Clark’s place on the list reflected her growing profile beyond basketball.

Clark’s arrival in the league in 2024 coincided with a substantial increase in attention. The WNBA drew more than 54 million unique viewers across national television networks during her rookie season, while total attendance rose 48% from the previous year.

The Fever also recorded 340,715 fans at home games, surpassing the New York Liberty’s previous league benchmark of 250,565, set in 2001. Clark wasn’t solely responsible for the league’s growth, but her popularity was an important factor.

Clark’s influence reaches far beyond the court

That audience interest has continued. In 2026, Fever games featuring Clark were among the most-watched WNBA broadcasts on CBS, ESPN and ION. An Indiana matchup against the Chicago Sky also became the second-most-watched WNBA game in ABC history, underscoring the star’s continuing drawing power.

The impact is visible on social media, too. Research by Indiana University Columbus finance professor Ryan Brewer found that official WNBA social-media views climbed from 373 million in late 2023 to nearly 2 billion by the end of the 2024 season, a 436% year-over-year increase.

Brewer compared the excitement around Clark to the “Taylor Swift effect,” while stressing that other players contribute to the league’s appeal. Clark’s highlights, he found, can attract far more views than typical WNBA game content.

Evert’s latest comment is consistent with her previous public support. When Clark was named TIME’s 2024 Athlete of the Year, Evert said she deserved the honor after Washington Mystics co-owner Sheila Johnson questioned the decision.

In June 2025, Evert also criticized poor sportsmanship after Clark was poked in the eye during a game against the Connecticut Sun.

Evert’s message is familiar, as she believes Clark’s popularity should be viewed as an opportunity. Recognizing one star doesn’t mean overlooking her teammates.

articles.title: Lexie Hull's emotional goodbye fuels uncertainty over Sophie Cunningham's Indiana Fever future
articles.standfirst: The player closed out her fifth season with the Fever with a message that sparked a flood of responses from Caitlin Clark, Aliyah Boston, and several of her teammates, although her future in Indiana is not in doubt.
articles.summary: The player closed out her fifth season with the Fever with a message that sparked a flood of responses from Caitlin Clark, Aliyah Boston, and several of her teammates, although her future in Indiana is not in doubt.
articles.body:
"L The season ended days ago for the Indiana Fever, but some of its leading figures are still processing a finish that came earlier than expected. Lexie Hull was one of them and used her social media to sum up what it meant to complete her fifth year with the franchise.

"Half a decade with Indiana Fever," Hull wrote alongside a carousel of photos from the season. The message was a reflection on her five years with the organization, but the tone of some of the replies made the post seem, at times, like a farewell.

Caitlin Clark, Aliyah Boston and the Fever react to Lexie Hull

Hull's teammates were quick to appear in the comments. Myisha Hines-Allen wrote "I already miss you", while Caitlin Clark replied with five pink hearts. Tyasha Harris left an "Lexxxxxx" accompanied by a heart.

Kelsey Mitchell and Aliyah Boston also took part. Mitchell used her teammate's nickname, "sexy lexi", while Boston wrote "I'm proud of you, sexyyyy lexiiii" Grace VanSlooten, Raven Johnson, and Monique Billings also joined in with messages.

The reaction makes sense because of the bond Hull has built with Indiana. The franchise selected her with the No. 6 pick in the 2022 Draft and since then she has played her entire WNBA career with the Fever.

In 2026, Hull started 41 games and averaged 5.2 points and 3.0 rebounds in 18.2 minutes per game.

The message doesn't mean Lexie Hull is leaving Indiana

Although the tone of the post may sound like a farewell, Hull is not saying goodbye to the Fever . Indiana agreed to a two-season contract extension with her worth around $1.6 million, so she is under contract through 2027.

What did come to an end was a season that left mixed feelings in Indianapolis. Indiana finished the regular season with a 28-16 record and placed sixth in the standings. In the playoffs, the Fever took their first-round series against the Las Vegas Aces to a third game, but were ultimately eliminated after losing 94-83.

Hull, therefore, has her continuity assured. The uncertainty lies in other pieces of the roster.

Sophie Cunningham, one of the pending decisions

The situation is especially interesting in the case of Sophie Cunningham, who faces an open future after her first full season with Indiana. Her continuity will be one of the decisions the franchise will have to address during the offseason.

Kelsey Mitchell's future, one of the team's main offensive references, also remains to be resolved as she enters free agency. Caitlin Clark herself publicly expressed her desire for Mitchell to remain in Indiana.

With Hull under contract through 2027, Clark and Aliyah Boston as central pieces, and several decisions still pending, Indiana faces an offseason with changes yet to be defined.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark’s “Taylor Swift effect” sent WNBA social views from 373 million to nearly 2 billion
articles.standfirst: A study found that views on the league’s official social media accounts more than quintupled after Clark’s rookie season
articles.summary: A study found that views on the league’s official social media accounts more than quintupled after Clark’s rookie season
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark’s impact is showing up somewhere beyond the box score: on fans’ screens. Views across the WNBA’s official social media accounts rose from 373 million in late 2023 to 1.96 billion after the 2024 season, according to a study by Indiana University Columbus finance professor Ryan Brewer. That’s more than five times the earlier total.

Brewer described the attention around Clark as a “Taylor Swift effect.” His comparison points to the kind of fascination that can draw people in beyond the usual audience. “People are fascinated by Clark,” he told The Indianapolis Star . The numbers don’t mean Clark alone accounts for the league’s growth: the study covers a season shaped by a celebrated rookie class, including Angel Reese, and the WNBA’s official accounts overall.

Clark’s highlights can turn a play into a viral moment

The scale is especially striking around Clark’s biggest plays. Brewer told the Star that highlights featuring Clark drew between 20 million and 45 million views across TikTok, X and Instagram, compared with roughly 3 million to 5 million for a WNBA game without her.

He said Clark generates 800% more viral views when her plays and highlights are featured. Those are view counts, not a tally of unique people.

The attention has carried into 2026. Brewer’s research found that Clark and the Fever generated more social media views than the rest of the league combined.

On television, Indiana’s Game 3 matchup with the Las Vegas Aces averaged 2.25 million viewers on USA Network and CNBC, making it the second most-watched first-round playoff game on record and the most-watched WNBA playoff game since 2024.

That is the larger story behind the “Taylor Swift effect”: one star can become an entry point to a whole league. Brewer stressed that basketball remains a team sport, and said fans are also noticing the other players around Clark.

The view counts show just how bright the spotlight has become. The league’s next challenge is to turn that attention into lasting interest that extends well beyond any one player by making the WNBA more competitive and, above all, fair and transparent.

articles.title: How much are Atlanta's and Golden State's players getting for making it to the WNBA Finals, and what is the prize money this year?
articles.standfirst: The Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries are competing for the 2026 WNBA championship
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries are competing for the 2026 WNBA championship
articles.body:
The Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries have reached the 2026 WNBA Finals, but the championship is about more than sporting glory.

With a new collective bargaining agreement in place, the players competing for the title are eligible for substantially larger financial bonuses than those available during last season’s playoffs.

Every player on the championship-winning team will receive a $60,000 bonus, while each player on the runner-up team is set to earn $20,000. The Finals Most Valuable Player will also receive an additional $30,000, making this year’s championship series particularly significant for the athletes involved.

The figures represent a considerable increase from 2025, when players on the winning team received $22,908 each and runners-up earned $8,521. The Finals MVP bonus has also risen from $5,000 to $30,000, giving the standout performer a much greater individual financial incentive.

For Atlanta and Golden State , therefore, the minimum financial reward for reaching the Finals is now considerably higher. Whichever team loses the best-of-seven series will still leave with the runner-up bonus, while the winners will receive three times as much per player.

articles.title: Angel Reese and Gabby Williams face off as the Atlanta Dream and Valkyries chase their first-ever title in the 2026 WNBA Finals
articles.standfirst: Golden State swept Atlanta in the regular season, but that was before the Dream added DeWanna Bonner
articles.summary: Golden State swept Atlanta in the regular season, but that was before the Dream added DeWanna Bonner
articles.body:
The 2026 WNBA Finals begin Saturday with a championship neither the Golden State Valkyries nor the Atlanta Dream have ever won. Golden State is playing for the title in just its second season, while Atlanta is back in the Finals for the first time since 2013. The series gives the league’s 30th season a new champion and two teams with very different paths to the same opportunity.

Atlanta arrives on a 10-game winning streak that stretches back to the regular season. The Dream swept the Washington Mystics in the first round and the New York Liberty in the semifinals. Golden State also swept its semifinal series, taking down the defending champion Las Vegas Aces, but needed three games to get past the Dallas Wings in the first round. The Valkyries are the first WNBA expansion team to reach the Finals in its second season.

The regular-season sweep may not tell the whole story

Golden State won all three regular-season games against Atlanta, holding the Dream to an average of 74.7 points. But those matchups took place in June and early July, and the teams haven’t faced each other since July 4.

Atlanta has also added veteran forward DeWanna Bonner since then. She has given the Dream more scoring and championship experience as they enter their first Finals in 13 years.

The teams’ defenses could shape every game. Atlanta’s Angel Reese, the WNBA Defensive Player of the Year , finished ahead of Golden State’s Gabby Williams in the voting. Both were named to the All-Defensive first team, alongside Dream guard Rhyne Howard.

Four of the six players who received votes for Defensive Player of the Year are in this series. The Dream create turnovers and convert them into points; the Valkyries make opponents work for nearly every shot.

Williams also gives the Finals a personal edge. The San Francisco native joined Golden State this season because she wanted to compete for a championship, and she has become one of the Valkyries’ most important players in the playoffs.

After the team’s home crowd helped power its run, she called Chase Center her “safe place.” Now she gets to lead the Valkyries into a Finals series in front of those fans.

Atlanta’s chances could also depend on Allisha Gray. The Dream’s leading scorer during the regular season missed the final two games of the semifinal sweep with a left-hand injury. On Thursday, Gray said she was “trending in the right direction” and hoped to play in Game 1, but Atlanta’s medical staff will make the final decision. Her availability matters against a Golden State defense that has made scoring difficult all season.

There is a home-court story in Atlanta, too. The Dream usually play at Gateway Center Arena, which seats about 3,500 fans. For the Finals, they moved Games 3 and 4 to State Farm Arena, with room for roughly 17,000.

The change followed a complicated scheduling puzzle involving a concert and an Atlanta Hawks game. It means the Dream will play their first Finals game in the Atlanta market since 2013 in front of a much larger crowd.

Game 1 is Saturday, Oct. 17, at 3:30 p.m. ET/12:30 p.m. PT at Chase Center in San Francisco, airing on NBC and Peacock. Game 2 is Monday, Oct. 19, before the series moves to Atlanta for Games 3 and 4. The best-of-seven matchup could run through Oct. 31, with a first championship waiting for whichever team wins four games.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham enraged by Angel Reese confrontation and referees' no-call
articles.standfirst: The Fever guard believes referees failed to maintain consistent standards after Reese’s heated exchanges with Liberty players
articles.summary: The Fever guard believes referees failed to maintain consistent standards after Reese’s heated exchanges with Liberty players
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham has voiced her frustration with the officiating in the WNBA playoffs, questioning why Angel Reese escaped punishment for several physical incidents during the Atlanta Dream’s semifinal series against the New York Liberty.

Speaking on her No Hesitation podcast ahead of the WNBA Finals, the Indiana Fever guard discussed Reese’s actions in Game 3, particularly her confrontation with Liberty guard Sabrina Ionescu following a hard offensive foul on Dream guard Isobel Borlase .

Although Cunningham acknowledged Reese’s willingness to stand up for her teammates, she argued that the officials should’ve issued a technical foul after the Chicago-born forward pursued Ionescu across the court and confronted her.

Cunningham believes players should be able to show emotion and defend their teammates, but she drew a distinction between verbal exchanges and actions that cross the line.

“Now, here we go … Angel, I appreciate her having her teammate’s back. I think that just shows that she care and that she has love for her teammates,” said Cunningham .

“Here’s my thing, if you’re going to chase someone down the court and get in someone’s ear, that should be a tech, any time. It’s going to be a tech in the regular season. Any other playoff games, that’s a technical foul. You can’t do that.

“Now if she were to stay on her side and kind of just yell and say something, I’m all for that. But the fact that she didn’t get a tech on that I think that is absolutely insane.”

Cunningham raises concerns over dangerous plays and inconsistent calls

The Fever guard also pointed to two other incidents involving Reese during Atlanta’s deciding semifinal game against New York, arguing that the officials overlooked potentially dangerous contact.

In one sequence, Reese made contact with Liberty star Breanna Stewart after the referees had already called a foul on Dream guard Rhyne Howard . Stewart was knocked to the floor, but Reese wasn’t penalized for the additional contact.

Another incident occurred early in the fourth quarter when Reese appeared to dive toward a loose ball following a timeout, making contact with the legs of Liberty guard Marine Fauthoux . Once again, the officials didn’t call a foul against her.

“You can’t tackle someone in the air and then go for someone’s knees and ankles. That’s a dangerous play,” Cunningham said, questioning why neither incident resulted in a penalty.

She also criticized the officials’ handling of an exchange between Reese and Liberty center Jonquel Jones . Both players received technical fouls after trading words, but Cunningham felt the penalties were unnecessary.

In her view, competitive trash talk should be allowed, provided players remain within the rules and avoid dangerous contact.

Cunningham further highlighted what she sees as a double standard by recalling her own technical foul for pointing during Indiana’s 86-77 victory over the Phoenix Mercury on June 22.

Atlanta advanced to the Finals after defeating New York 85-83 in Game 3, while Indiana’s campaign ended with a 94-83 loss to the Las Vegas Aces.

The Dream are now preparing to face the Golden State Valkyries in Game 1 of the best-of-seven WNBA Finals at San Francisco’s Chase Center on Saturday.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark merch sparks Atlanta Dream fan’s outrage at Nike store ahead of WNBA Finals
articles.standfirst: A fan filmed Clark’s display taking a more prominent spot than Atlanta
articles.summary: A fan filmed Clark’s display taking a more prominent spot than Atlanta
articles.body:
The Atlanta Dream are preparing for the WNBA Finals, but one fan says their merchandise barely showed it. In a video from the Nike Store at Lenox Square, Caitlin Clark gear appears prominently displayed while Dream merchandise sits off to the side.

“We are in the WNBA Finals, the ATL merch needs to be switched with CC,” the fan says. She then records herself leaving the store without buying any Dream gear. Her complaint captures a sharp contrast: Atlanta is still playing for a title, while Indiana’s season is over but Clark’s merchandise appeared to get the prime spot.

Atlanta has the better playoff run. Clark has the merch numbers

On the court, the Dream have earned the spotlight. They swept Washington in the first round and New York in the semifinals, reaching the Finals with a 5-0 playoff record. The Fever were eliminated by Las Vegas in a 2-1 first-round series. In its 2024 impact report, published in March 2025, the WNBA said jersey sales had jumped 801% year over year and that Clark was the league’s top seller across Fanatics’ network, behind only MLB star Shohei Ohtani among athletes.

There are signs the Dream’s merchandise business is growing. Yahoo Sports reported that Atlanta ranked second in retail growth last year and among the league’s top five teams in overall retail sales. This season, the team partnered with Monarch Commerce to expand its merchandise operation and launch new apparel, including a Nike uniform and an Atlanta-inspired collection.

The display also appeared just after Nike launched Clark’s first signature shoe and apparel collection on Oct. 1. That timing offers a possible reason for the prominent Clark merchandise, though it does not explain the store’s decision or establish how its sales compare with Dream gear.

Atlanta has made the Finals, but a single store’s display reflects more than the standings. Product launches, inventory and customer demand can all shape what gets shelf space. The video can’t settle which team sells more, but it shows why the fan felt the Dream deserved better.

Game 1 of the WNBA Finals is Saturday, Oct. 17, with the Atlanta Dream visiting the Golden State Valkyries at Chase Center in San Francisco. Tipoff is scheduled for 3:30 p.m. ET/12:30 p.m. PT, with coverage on NBC and Peacock. Game 2 will be played Monday, Oct. 19, at 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT on USA Network, CNBC and Peacock.

articles.title: Angel Reese makes her WNBA Finals debut as the league’s most-followed player even surpassing Caitlin Clark
articles.standfirst: Although Reese and Cunningham are the most famous on social media, Clark is the most popular worldwide.
articles.summary: Although Reese and Cunningham are the most famous on social media, Clark is the most popular worldwide.
articles.body:
The 30th WNBA season reaches its climax as the Atlanta Dream prepare to square off against the Golden State Valkyries in the WNBA Finals .

The Bay Area expansion franchise reaches its first championship series in just its second season in the league after dethroning the reigning champion Las Vegas Aces , while Atlanta searches for its first title in four Finals appearances after downing the 2024 champion New York Liberty.

Both rosters are deeply balanced and exceptionally coached, setting up what could easily become a seven-game classic. The series tips off at the Chase Center , making Golden State the first team in league history to average over 18,000 fans in their home venue, affectionately dubbed "Ballhalla."

Meanwhile, Atlanta will host Games 3, 4, and 6 (if necessary) at State Farm Arena after finalizing an agreement with the Atlanta Hawks, who open their regular season next week.

Angel Reese Leads Social Media Rankings

The championship series features the league's most followed player on social media: reigning Defensive Player of the Year Angel Reese .

Boasting 5.3 million followers on Instagram and 6.7 million on TikTok , Reese stands as the top social media presence in women's basketball, surpassing Indiana Fever stars Sophie Cunningham (4.3 million Instagram / 4.5 million TikTok) and Caitlin Clark (4.3 million Instagram / 1.2 million TikTok), as well as Paige Bueckers (3.1 million Instagram / 4.0 million TikTok).

These four stand as the only players across the league with over 5 million combined followers across platforms . Reese has capitalized on her cultural stardom off the court, and now in her first season in Atlanta, she has the opportunity to capture her first professional title.

However, while Reese holds the digital edge in total follower counts, Caitlin Clark remains the single largest television draw on the planet, evidenced by the fact that all 10 of the most-watched games this season featured the Fever.

The contrast lies in digital activity: Reese and Cunningham engage daily on social platforms, whereas Clark maintains a significantly quieter online profile.

articles.title: Angel Reese drives fans wild with behind-the-scenes look at collaboration ahead of WNBA Finals
articles.standfirst: The basketball star grabbed attention with a post that comes at a crucial point in her season.
articles.summary: The basketball star grabbed attention with a post that comes at a crucial point in her season.
articles.body:
T he WNBA Finals tip off this Saturday, October 17, but Angel Reese also has exciting news off the court . The basketball star shared a behind-the-scenes video of her collaboration with Reebok and Reese’s, which turned the famous candy brand’s colors into a special-edition sneaker.

Although the collection was announced in September 2026, the new footage offers a closer look at the Reebok Angel Reese 1 and the photo shoot featuring the Atlanta Dream star.

Angel Reese shows off her Reese’s-inspired sneakers

For the shoot, Reese opted for a brown outfit, a matching jacket, her hair pulled back into a ponytail, and gold earrings. However, the sneakers stole much of the spotlight thanks to their distinctive color combination .

The orange laces and brand logos on the tongue and insoles reinforce the visual connection to Reese’s. The release also includes a special orange box designed to accompany the launch.

The Reebok Angel Reese 1 sneakers are built for the court, too

Beyond their appearance, the sneakers feature basketball-focused technology, including Reebok’s Energy Return System (ERS), SuperFloat cushioning made with nitrogen-infused foam, and a TPU heel structure designed to provide support and stability.

The choice of Reese’s also reflects Reese’s connection with her fans. Some call her “Reese’s Pieces,” a nickname that plays on her last name and the candy brand. This connection gives the collaboration a personal touch for the basketball star, making it more than just a combination of two brands’ colors.

The Reebok Angel Reese 1 sneakers will go on sale in the United States on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, at 10 a.m. ET, three days after the WNBA Finals begin .

Atlanta have won all five of their playoff games, with Reese playing a central role as the former LSU Tigers standout is averaging 18.0 points and 8.4 rebounds per game in the playoffs, helping the Dream sweep both the Washington Mystics and the New York Liberty .

Reese delivered with a team-high 22 points in the decisive semifinal victory over New York , and her performances have now earned her another title, CJ McCollum referring to Reese as the Queen of the South ahead of the championship series. “Obviously, the Atlanta team changed when the Queen of the South got here,” McCollum said. “So happy for her, happy to see them doing well, happy to see the team in the city kind of surrounding them.” Reese thanked the ex- NBA star for the recognition and suggesting the nickname reflects her connection to Louisiana , where she became a college basketball star at LSU . “Shoutout to CJ McCollum. It is really cool when you men’s team shows love to you,” Reese said. “I guess he’s saying that because I played at LSU. I appreciate the name. I guess that’s my new nickname – Queen of the South.” The latest title joins her established Bayou Barbie and Chi Barbie nicknames, the former emerging during her time at LSU in Baton Rouge , as she helped lead the college to a national championship in 2023. Chi Barbie followed after the Chicago Sky selected her seventh overall in the 2024 WNBA Draft , while Baltimore Barbie has paid tribute to her hometown in Maryland .

Reese readies for Game 1 of the WNBA Finals

Now Reese has an opportunity to turn her growing profile into a championship. The Dream face a formidable Golden State team that has made history by reaching the Finals in just its second season, following its debut in 2025. The Valkyries became the first expansion franchise to reach the playoffs in its inaugural campaign and have continued that progress under coach Natalie Nakase , whilst Gabby Williams has helped lead Golden State , averaging 14.4 points, 3.3 rebounds and 1.6 steals. The Finals could be decided by defensive execution, with the two teams accounting for six of the WNBA 's 10 All-Defensive selections. Tamika Catchings has highlighted defensive health as a major factor. Atlanta , meanwhile, is waiting on the status of leading scorer Allisha Gray , who injured her shooting hand during the semifinal series and reportedly underwent a minor procedure during the break. Game 1 tips off Saturday, October 17, at 15:30 ET/12:30 PT at Chase Center in San Francisco .

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham accused of hypocrisy: Fans expose her history of dirty tricks in defending Angel Reese
articles.standfirst: The Indiana Fever player has earned a reputation for defending Caitlin Clark
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever player has earned a reputation for defending Caitlin Clark
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham has sparked backlash after criticizing Angel Reese for her physical play during the Atlanta Dream 's WNBA semifinal series against the New York Liberty as fans quickly pointed to her own controversial history, particularly a notorious takedown of Jacy Sheldon in 2025. The Indiana Fever guard addressed Reese 's confrontation with Sabrina Ionescu ahead of Game 1 of the WNBA Finals , arguing the Dream forward should have received a technical foul for chasing down her opponent and getting in her face in a Game 3 incident vs. the Liberty .

“I appreciate her having her teammate’s back,” Cunningham said on the No Hesitation podcast. “I think that just shows that she care and that she has love for her teammates. Here’s my thing, if you’re going to chase someone down the court and get in someone’s ear, that should be a tech, any time.” Cunningham argued that officials would have penalized the behavior during the regular season and questioned why Reese escaped punishment in the playoffs. She then went further, accusing the Atlanta star of dangerous contact during games. “Angel is going to play hard. But you can’t tackle someone in the air and go for someone’s knees and ankles,” Cunningham said as the comments quickly drew criticism from Reese 's supporters, who questioned whether she was applying the same standards to herself that she expected from others. One fan wrote on X: “The call is coming from inside of the house. When has Angel ever tackled someone…let alone in the air??” Whilst a second said, “She has nothing else going for herself but rage bait and bold face lying at this point.”

Sophie Cunningham's Jacy Sheldon takedown returns to haunt her

Another referenced Cunningham 's confrontation with Sheldon , and it’s true that the Fever player’s own history of physical confrontations has become central to the criticism as in June 2025, she was ejected after taking down the Connecticut Sun player. The incident followed an earlier flashpoint in which Sheldon accidentally poked Caitlin Clark in the eye during defensive contact. Then with the Fever comfortably ahead in the final minute, Cunningham intervened as her rival drove toward the basket. Wrapping her up and bringing her to the floor, officials assessed Cunningham a Flagrant 2 foul and ejected her whilst Sheldon and Connecticut guard Lindsay Allen were also ejected after the confrontation escalated. The incident raised questions about whether Cunningham was protecting Clark or retaliating against Sheldon as she defended her actions by arguing that Indiana needed to protect its star, while critics viewed the takedown as excessive and potentially dangerous. The WNBA issued Cunningham an additional fine, but no suspension and the episode nevertheless strengthened her reputation as Clark 's self-appointed “enforcer,” a label embraced by some Fever supporters and criticized by others.

articles.title: Draymond Green's bold verdict on the WNBA: People are paying premium prices just to watch Angel Reese fail
articles.standfirst: The Warriors star claims some fans are tuning in to see Reese fail, but their attention could be giving the WNBA an unexpected boost
articles.summary: The Warriors star claims some fans are tuning in to see Reese fail, but their attention could be giving the WNBA an unexpected boost
articles.body:
A ngel Reese's ability to attract attention is becoming a major talking point ahead of the 2026 WNBA Finals.

According to Golden State Warriors forward Draymond Green , however, not everyone tuning in to watch the Atlanta Dream star will be hoping she lifts the championship trophy. Some viewers, he believes, are equally interested in seeing her struggle on basketball's biggest stage.

Speaking On the October 16 episode of The Draymond Green Show, Green discussed how Reese's polarizing reputation has helped her become one of the most talked-about players in women's basketball.

“Angel is gonna have people watching this because there’s a large consortium of people who want to see her succeed,” Green said. “There’s an even larger group of people who want to see her fail, and they’re gonna watch to see her fail, which is great.

“Great. Come on. Come watch for the league. It’s great. But they’re going to watch because they want to see her fail. So, I think that also brings something to this matchup.”

His comments arrive at a time when interest in the championship series is translating into unusually high ticket prices.

Atlanta will face the Golden State Valkyries in a matchup that offers both franchises an opportunity to capture their first WNBA title.

According to Front Office Sports, the cheapest tickets listed for Game 1 at San Francisco's Chase Center stood at $214 on October 15.

That's a considerable increase from last year's Finals opener between the Las Vegas Aces and Phoenix Mercury, when the lowest-priced ticket reportedly ended at just $34. Atlanta's Game 3 also generated significant demand, with reported entry prices reaching $201.

Angel Reese is ready to embrace the championship spotlight

Although Reese's public profile has attracted plenty of criticism, her performances have given Atlanta another reason to celebrate.

The Dream are pursuing their first championship after a lengthy wait, and their star forward has played an important role in their postseason campaign.

Through five playoff games, Reese is averaging 18.0 points, 8.4 rebounds, 2.2 blocks, 2.0 assists and 1.6 steals. She's also shooting 38.5% from beyond the arc, while her defensive presence has helped Atlanta establish itself as a formidable playoff team.

Reaching the Finals represents an opportunity for Reese to demonstrate that she can deliver when the stakes are highest.

Speaking during Friday's media day, she made it clear that she's prepared for the challenge.

“You have to be a playoff riser,” Reese said. “The greats are built for this. If you want to be considered the best player and well-respected, you can't shy away from the moment.”

The forward can draw on previous championship experience, having won the 2023 NCAA title with LSU and earned a gold medal with Team USA at the World Cup in Berlin in September.

Reese has consistently emphasized her determination to win, regardless of the circumstances. Now, she'll have the opportunity to put that mindset to the test against Golden State.

Reese's performances will offer the clearest response to her critics. With a championship within reach, she has an opportunity to turn the spotlight into a defining moment.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark plans to get “very involved” as the Fever prepare for a pivotal offseason
articles.standfirst: The Fever's first priority is to bring Kelsey Mitchell back
articles.summary: The Fever's first priority is to bring Kelsey Mitchell back
articles.body:
he WNBA Finals begin tonight with two franchise programs locked in pursuit of their first title: the Golden State Valkyries , making a historic run in just their second season in the league, and the Atlanta Dream , making their fourth Finals appearance in franchise history.

Under the best-of-seven format, Golden State will host Games 1, 2, 5, and 7 (if necessary), while Atlanta is scheduled to host Games 3, 4, and 6 (if necessary), setting up the season to officially conclude on October 31st in the event of a Game 7.

However, as the championship series tips off, the offseason looms large for the rest of the league, featuring a loaded free-agent market with marquee names like Napheesa Collier , Kelsey Plum , Jackie Young , and the Indiana Fever duo of Kelsey Mitchell and Sophie Cunningham .

Mitchell, in particular, expects a massive market of suitors following an MVP-caliber season alongside Caitlin Clark, an explosive backcourt tandem that propelled the Fever to a league-record 96.0 points per game and an all-time high of 4,222 total points scored across the campaign.

Caitlin Clark Takes Active Leadership Role for the Fever Free Agency Pursuit

After suffering a second consecutive playoff exit at the hands of the Las Vegas Aces, the Indiana Fever enter a pivotal transition period with only six players under contract heading into the winter.

Recognizing the urgency to construct a true contender, Caitlin Clark addressed her role in pitch meetings and roster discussions during her end-of-season exit interview, expressing a firm commitment to help recruit high-level free agents and showcase the city of Indianapolis.

"I think this offseason will be a little bit different, and I'll be very involved in that," Clark emphasized. Re-signing Mitchell remains top priority for the front office, but should talks stall, targeting elite two-way talent like Napheesa Collier could be game-changing.

Pairing Collier with Aliyah Boston would instantly form a formidable interior defensive tandem to balance Indiana's high-powered attack.

Though injuries limited Collier to 18 games last season, her previous two campaigns yielded 2024 Defensive Player of the Year honors and back-to-back top-two MVP finishes while averaging 21.6 points and 8.5 rebounds per game .

Having Clark directly engaged in the pitch process gives Indiana a compelling pitch to land game-changing talent capable of pushing the franchise past its recent postseason plateau.

articles.title: Angel Reese stuns with her look for the start of the WNBA Finals despite losing Game 1
articles.standfirst: It was a tough day for the Dream.
articles.summary: It was a tough day for the Dream.
articles.body:
This Saturday, October 17, the Golden State Valkyries defeated the Atlanta Dream 68-64 at Chase Center in San Francisco, California , to take the lead in the WNBA Finals. The game came down to a four-point difference, leaving Angel Reese and her teammates looking for a comeback in the next matchup.

​Angel Reese records a double-double in Game 1 of the Finals

Although the Atlanta Dream fell short of victory, Angel Reese got off to a strong start, scoring 11 points in the first quarter as her team took control early. The basketball star finished with 14 points and 12 rebounds, including five offensive boards, along with two steals and one block in 35 minutes of action .

However, personal fouls complicated her performance. Reese picked up five and had to leave the court at a crucial moment as Atlanta tried to stay in contention. She also recorded four turnovers and made five of her 11 field-goal attempts .

Allisha Gray led the Dream's offense with 19 points, but the team managed just eight points in the fourth quarter. On the other side, Gabby Williams starred with 26 points to lead the Golden State Valkyries to the series-opening win.

Angel Reese's look steals the spotlight at the start of the WNBA Finals

Beyond the action on the court, Reese also turned heads before tipoff in a cream-colored tracksuit with black details, paired with sophisticated accessories.

Her zip-up jacket featured dark stripes along the sleeves and matched wide-leg pants with a relaxed fit. Narrow, oval black sunglasses gave her outfit a 2000s-inspired vibe, while a wide headband kept her hair pulled back into a high, voluminous ponytail .

To complete the look, she chose a structured black handbag with a flap and gold hardware, long earrings, and sleek black shoes. The accessories added an elegant touch without taking away from the sporty inspiration behind her outfit .

With this sporty-chic ensemble, the Dream star showed how to elevate athletic staples with accessories that make any outfit stand out.

The Atlanta Dream will face the Golden State Valkyries again on Monday, October 19, at Chase Center in San Francisco. Tipoff is scheduled for 8 p.m. ET .

articles.title: Gabby Williams leads the Valkyries to their first victory in the WNBA Finals against Angel Reese
articles.standfirst: Scores 26 points and is decisive in the final stretch
articles.summary: Scores 26 points and is decisive in the final stretch
articles.body:
Unbeatable debut for Gabby Williams and the Golden State Valkyries in the WNBA Finals . With a superb performance, the fourth best by a rookie in the Finals, Williams led her team in the first game for the title against the Atlanta Dream, 68-64 in a packed Chase Center with 18,064 spectators.

Those of San Francisco only went ahead in the game in the final 100 seconds, choosing their moment perfectly. A 7 -0 run in the final 2:15 gave the home team the win in their first game in the NBA Finals . It should be remembered that the Valkyries are a team with only two years of existence.

Born in Reno but with a French passport (in fact she plays for France), Gabby Williams was the star of the game. She scored 26 points, the fourth-best total for a rookie in the Finals , but six of those points came during the 7-0 run with which Golden State sealed the game.

In those final two minutes, the Atlanta Dream missed all their shots, including five three-pointers, while Williams made all six free throws she attempted, putting her team ahead on the scoreboard to win.

' It's very nice, but I feel like we still haven't finished the job ,' said Williams when asked how she felt hearing the entire arena chant her name. ' Even when we were behind, I thought we had the game where I wanted it,' said the player of the game against the Dream .'

Williams was the only Valkyries player to score in double figures. She was followed by Kiah Stokes with 9 points and 7 rebounds. For Atlanta, Alisha Gray scored 19, Angel Reese 14, and Rhyne Howard 12. The second game will also be played at the Chase Center in the early hours of Tuesday to Wednesday at 2:00.

articles.title: Angel Reese takes responsibility after second-half disappearance in WNBA Finals opener
articles.standfirst: The Atlanta Dream star scored 11 points in the first quarter but went quiet after halftime as the Golden State Valkyries stole Game 1
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream star scored 11 points in the first quarter but went quiet after halftime as the Golden State Valkyries stole Game 1
articles.body:
Angel Reese didn't point fingers after the Atlanta Dream let the opening game of the 2026 WNBA Finals slip away.

Instead, the star forward turned the spotlight on herself after a second-half scoring drought helped the Golden State Valkyries secure a 68-64 victory on Saturday.

Atlanta appeared to be in control for much of the contest at Chase Center. Reese gave the Dream an early spark, scoring 11 points in the first quarter as her team built a substantial advantage.

But the Valkyries gradually fought their way back into the game, and Atlanta couldn't find enough offense down the stretch to protect its lead.

Reese finished with 14 points, 12 rebounds, two steals and one block, recording another double-double on the biggest stage of her young career.

Yet her final line told only part of the story. After making an immediate impact early, she failed to score in the second half, leaving Atlanta without one of its most important offensive options when the game tightened.

Asked after the loss what Golden State had done to limit her production, Reese rejected the idea that the Valkyries deserved all the credit for her quiet finish.

"I don't think they really did anything," Reese said. "Maybe that's just on me. I wasn't aggressive enough with the ball and trying to get the ball and get to my spots."

Her response placed the emphasis on what she could change rather than on the opposing defense. It also offered a clear indication of what she wants to correct before the teams meet again.

Atlanta offense stalled as Golden State found opening

The shot numbers help explain Reese 's frustration. She attempted nine shots in the first half, making five of them, but took only two attempts across nearly 18 minutes after the break.

For a player who had established herself as an early scoring threat, that dramatic drop in involvement became a significant problem for Atlanta.

Reese 's ability to attack the paint and create second chances is central to the Dream 's identity. Her rebounding gives Atlanta extra possessions, while her physical presence near the basket can force defenses to adjust.

When she stops looking for her own shot, however, opponents can devote more attention to the team's other scorers.

Golden State took advantage of the changing momentum. Gabby Williams delivered a game-high 26 points, including crucial free throws late in the fourth quarter, to help the Valkyries complete the comeback.

No other Golden State player reached double figures, but the team's bench outscored Atlanta's reserves 20-6, providing a major advantage in a tightly contested game.

Allisha Gray led Atlanta with 19 points, while Rhyne Howard added 12. Even with those contributions, the Dream struggled to generate consistent offense late in the game. Atlanta scored only eight points in the fourth quarter and missed several opportunities to reclaim the lead in the closing minutes.

The result was particularly frustrating because the Dream had put themselves in a strong position. They entered the final period ahead by five points, but Golden State 's defensive pressure and late execution changed the outcome.

articles.body:
The Golden State Valkyries claimed the opening victory of the WNBA Finals, but two contentious plays involving Angel Reese have become a major talking point following the Atlanta Dream 's 68-64 defeat.

Reese entered the championship series hoping to help Atlanta secure its first WNBA title, having played an important role in the team's unbeaten run through the earlier playoff rounds.

However, the three-time All-Star found herself facing criticism after making contact with two Golden State players during a physical second half at Chase Center.

The incidents involving Gabby Williams and Veronica Burton prompted allegations that the referees failed to adequately penalize Reese , although the available accounts differ on whether an offensive foul was assessed during the first play.

Reese elbow to Williams sparks controversy

The first disputed incident occurred during the third quarter when Williams challenged Reese for possession as the Atlanta forward attempted to protect the basketball.

Reese turned while battling for control, and her elbow struck Williams in the face, prompting an immediate reaction from viewers following the game.

A separate incident followed when Reese attempted to contest a layup by Burton , approaching from behind before making contact with the guard's face.

WNBA reporter Robin Lundberg criticized the officiating after watching the sequences, suggesting that both incidents warranted penalties.

"Refs let Angel Reese get away with two blatant fouls, no call," Lundberg wrote on X.

His assessment generated further discussion about the standard of officiating during the postseason, particularly when physical contact involves players attempting to protect possession or challenge shots.

Fans question officials after controversial plays

"100%. She is the Draymond of the WNBA," one fan wrote, comparing her physical style to that of NBA forward Draymond Green .

Another supporter claimed Reese had repeatedly avoided consequences for excessive contact, although no evidence was presented to establish preferential treatment by officials.

The latest controversy follows criticism surrounding Atlanta's semifinal series against the New York Liberty , when Reese made contact with Breanna Stewart during another physical sequence.

Officials reviewed that incident and determined there had been no hostile act, allowing play to continue without additional punishment.

articles.standfirst: Freedom is preparing another public protest after previous WNBA appearance ended in arena ban and legal dispute
articles.summary: Freedom is preparing another public protest after previous WNBA appearance ended in arena ban and legal dispute
articles.body:
With the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries preparing for Game 3 of the WNBA Finals, former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom has announced plans to attend Wednesday's matchup with a message that could reignite an already contentious debate.

Freedom confirmed that he will be at State Farm Arena on October 21, promising to unveil a new t-shirt as part of his ongoing campaign against the WNBA's transgender athlete eligibility policies.

The announcement follows his controversial declaration for the 2027 WNBA Draft, a symbolic move intended to challenge the league's eligibility requirements rather than establish a realistic playing opportunity.

However, his latest video went beyond policy criticism, with Freedom directing personal remarks toward two of the Finals' most prominent players.

Freedom explained that his campaign began after hearing comments from Valkyries star Gabby Williams supporting transgender athletes competing in women's basketball.

"As you all know, this all started with an interview featuring Gabby Williams of the Golden State Valkyries, when she said, 'I have no problem with trans athletes playing on my team or against my team,'" Freedom said in a video posted on X.

"Her words gave me so much hope and motivation to come out as a woman and officially declare for the WNBA Draft."

Freedom subsequently shifted his attention to Dream forward Angel Reese , claiming she had blocked him on social media.

"My favorite diva has unfortunately blocked me on social media. But that won't stop me from showing my appreciation for the one and only Angel Reese," he said.

"I can't wait to take some notes on how to finish a layup after grabbing a rebound."

The remarks continue Freedom 's pattern of using provocative public statements to draw attention to his opposition to the league's policies.

Previous WNBA protest ended in legal dispute

Freedom 's upcoming appearance follows an incident at Wintrust Arena during an August 23 game between the Chicago Sky and Indiana Fever .

The former NBA center attended wearing a black t-shirt displaying the definition "WOMAN noun. adult human female," prompting attention from spectators and players.

During the third quarter, Sky guard Natasha Cloud approached Freedom following a basket, with the pair exchanging words before security intervened.

Freedom was subsequently ejected and banned from the arena. He later filed a lawsuit challenging his removal, alleging that his First Amendment rights had been violated. The dispute remains a significant backdrop to his latest plans.

Freedom promises surprise at WNBA Finals Game 3

Freedom has refused to reveal the message on his latest t-shirt, instead suggesting that fans should expect something memorable.

"Everyone keeps asking me the same question: 'What t-shirt are you going to wear this time?'" he said. "Well, let me tell you something — this one is going to blow your minds!"

He also claimed he intends to watch the Finals to assess potential competition before his proposed entry into the league next year.

His draft declaration doesn't establish that he meets the WNBA's eligibility requirements, and there's no confirmed prospect of him participating in the 2027 season.

The immediate focus, however, remains Wednesday's championship matchup, where Reese and Williams will be attempting to help their respective teams move closer to the title.

articles.standfirst: Angel Reese and Wendell Carter Jr. have become one of sports’ most talked-about couples, but their championship pursuits could soon put them on separate stages.
articles.summary: Angel Reese and Wendell Carter Jr. have become one of sports’ most talked-about couples, but their championship pursuits could soon put them on separate stages.
articles.body:
A ngel Reese and Wendell Carter Jr. have established themselves as one of the most followed couples in American sports. While the Atlanta Dream star is chasing a WNBA Finals championship, the Orlando Magic center is putting the finishing touches on his preparation for the start of a new NBA season.

With Orlando set to make its season debut on October 21 against the Atlanta Hawks , it remains unclear whether Carter will be able to join Reese during the championship series.

In an interview with Brandon "Scoop B" Robinson , the Magic big man explained that much of his summer was split between preparing physically for the new season and constantly supporting his girlfriend.

“It’s been a great summer. A lot of hard work, a lot of relaxation, and a lot of support for my girl,” Carter said.

“It’s been good, man,” Carter said of the offseason.

The former Duke standout also revealed that the two maintain constant communication to help each other improve on the court.

“We’re both competitors,” Carter said.

Before Carter, Reese was linked to Jalen Duren

Before beginning her relationship with Wendell Carter Jr. , Angel Reese was romantically linked to Detroit Pistons cente r Jalen Duren in 2024 .

Rumors about her relationship with Carter began circulating in 2025 , and although the couple has never officially announced their romance, they have publicly shown the support they provide each other in their respective careers.

On the court, Reese is looking to win the first WNBA championship of her career. Her move from the Chicago Sky to the Atlanta Dream has represented a major boost for her development as a player.

“You have to rise in the playoffs,” Reese said ahead of the Finals.

“The great players are built for these moments. If you want to be considered one of the best and earn everyone’s respect, you can’t shy away when the biggest moments arrive.”

articles.standfirst: Reese delivered a historic performance with 30 points and 16 rebounds to help Atlanta steal Game 2 and even the WNBA Finals.
articles.summary: Reese delivered a historic performance with 30 points and 16 rebounds to help Atlanta steal Game 2 and even the WNBA Finals.
articles.body:
A ngel Reese delivered one of the greatest performances in WNBA Finals history , exploding for 30 points and 16 rebounds to lead the Atlanta Dream to a 79-65 victory over the Golden State Valkyries on Monday night, evening the best-of-seven championship series at 1-1 .

Allisha Gray added 18 points, while Jordin Canada recorded a near triple-double with 13 points, 10 assists and seven rebounds. On the defensive end, Rhyne Howard set a new WNBA Finals record with six steals as Atlanta overwhelmed Golden State after halftime.

The win was historic for the Dream, marking the franchise's first-ever WNBA Finals victory after losing its previous 10 Finals games across three appearances. Atlanta now heads home with momentum after stealing a split in front of Golden State's sold-out "Ballhalla" crowd at Chase Center.

“This environment is tough to play in. Shoutout to the fans. Shoutout my team, though,” Reese said. “We came and fought. Game 1 was tough for us, but we moved on.”

Reese also entered elite company, becoming just the third player in WNBA Finals history to record at least 30 points and 15 rebounds in a Finals game , joining Jonquel Jones (2019) and Breanna Stewart (2020) .

“She was definitely way more aggressive. She had a great game,” Valkyries center Kiah Stokes admitted. “We let everyone kind of have their way.”

Game 3 shifts to Atlanta on Wednesday, where the next two Finals games will be played at State Farm Arena, home of the NBA's Hawks, allowing more than 17,000 fans to attend instead of the Dream's usual 3,500-seat venue.

Golden State never found its rhythm offensively. Gabby Williams led the Valkyries with 14 points, but shot just 3-for-15 after scoring 26 in Game 1. As a team, the Valkyries shot 34.4% from the field and 7-of-24 from beyond the arc.

“We shot terribly,” guard Veronica Burton said. “We missed shots that we make all the time.”

After being held scoreless in the second half of Game 1, Reese responded with a dominant all-around performance, shooting 10-for-16 from the field while adding three assists and two blocks.

“We watched film and saw the things that we messed up on,” Reese said. “When I said they didn’t do anything to mess us up, it was literally just us. You could see that tonight. We’re going to carry that over to Atlanta. Atlanta, y’all better pull up—I’m looking forward to it.”

Atlanta's defense proved to be the difference, forcing 19 turnovers and converting them into 24 points, a dramatic improvement from the eight points off turnovers the Dream managed in Game 1 . The victory also handed the Valkyries their first regulation loss since Aug. 21, snapping one of the league's hottest streaks at the biggest stage.

articles.standfirst: The Atlanta Dream star delivered 30 points and 16 rebounds but appeared frustrated
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream star delivered 30 points and 16 rebounds but appeared frustrated
articles.body:
The Atlanta Dream needed a response after losing the opening game of the WNBA Finals , and Angel Reese delivered one of the finest performances of her career to help restore their championship hopes.

Reese scored 30 points and collected 16 rebounds as Atlanta defeated the Golden State Valkyries 79-65 on Monday night, leveling the best-of-seven series at one game apiece.

The performance made Reese the first player in Dream history to register at least 25 points and 10 rebounds in a WNBA Finals game, underlining her growing influence on the championship stage.

However, the celebration was accompanied by an uncomfortable moment when Reese appeared to lose patience with her teammates during the third quarter, despite already being Atlanta's most productive player.

The incident occurred with just under eight minutes remaining in the third quarter as Atlanta worked through an offensive possession.

Reese positioned herself in the mid-range area and signaled repeatedly that she was available, raising her hand in an attempt to attract attention from the ball handler.

Rather than deliver the pass, her teammates continued moving the ball around the perimeter, leaving Reese visibly frustrated as the possession developed without her involvement.

The forward responded by placing her hands on her hips and stamping her foot before moving toward the area near Atlanta's bench.

Her reaction became particularly noticeable when Allisha Gray attempted a three-pointer that failed to find the basket, with Reese appearing disengaged from the play.

As players regrouped, teammate Te-Hina Paopao approached Reese for a high-five, but the forward appeared to ignore the gesture.

Reese responds with historic WNBA Finals performance

Despite that moment, Reese remained the driving force behind Atlanta's victory, delivering the offensive production the Dream had lacked during their narrow Game 1 defeat.

Her 30 points led all Atlanta players, while her 16 rebounds gave the team a significant presence around the basket.

Reese also recorded three assists and converted 10 of 16 attempts from mid-range, along with her only three-point opportunity.

Her contribution was particularly important as Atlanta attempted to contain a Golden State team that had entered Monday's matchup holding the early advantage in the series.

Gabby Williams and Tiffany Hayes led the Valkyries with 14 points each, but neither could match Reese's overall influence.

Meanwhile, Jordin Canada provided much of Atlanta's offensive organization, finishing with 10 assists.

Dream gain momentum before return home

The victory sends the championship series to Atlanta level at 1-1, giving the Dream an opportunity to take control in front of their home supporters.

Game 3 is scheduled for Wednesday, October 21, at State Farm Arena, with Atlanta also hosting the following matchup.

Reese 's emotional third-quarter reaction will attract attention, but her overall performance demonstrated why she has become central to the Dream 's championship ambitions.

The forward combined scoring efficiency with dominant rebounding, helping Atlanta respond to its opening defeat and restore momentum.

With the series finely balanced, Reese 's ability to sustain that level of production could prove far more consequential than a brief moment of frustration.

Game 3 is scheduled for Wednesday, October 21, at State Farm Arena, with Atlanta also hosting the following matchup.

The forward combined scoring efficiency with dominant rebounding, helping Atlanta respond to its opening defeat and restore momentum.

articles.summary: Reese delivered a statement performance on the biggest stage, then let her celebration do the talking
articles.body:
A ngel Reese is living the dream of any young basketball player. She is one of the most criticized figures in the WNBA, but she is also someone who makes sure her personality shines through when things go her way.

Among the new generation of players becoming the face of the league, Reese could become the first to win a WNBA title , even before Caitlin Clark, whom many had tipped as the favorite to reach that milestone. So when Reese delivers results that people did not expect, she lets her hips do the talking and her attitude make the statement.

Reese backs up her confidence on the court

Atlanta did more than tie the series. Reese took center stage with her confidence, scoring and ability to fire up her team when her game was clicking. The Dream responded by continuing to feed her, with Reese scoring 12 points in her final 12 minutes. Atlanta built a lead of as many as 21 points in the fourth quarter before closing out a 79-65 win over the Golden State Valkyries on Monday.

Reese was outstanding, carrying the team with one of the strongest performances of her season. She finished with 30 points, 16 rebounds, two blocks and one steal, delivering a performance that answered her critics on the league’s biggest stage.

Her celebration sends a message to the haters

After the win, Reese broke into a dance that showed just how much she was enjoying the moment . It was a celebration of her performance and a reminder that she is not ready to stop here.

With the series tied at one game apiece, Reese has more to chase . Her dance made it clear that she wants everything the WNBA Finals have to offer, and she was not about to hide her confidence from those who have doubted her along the way.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham Speaks Out About Angel Reese: “Her Offensive Game Is Going to Improve”
articles.standfirst: The Indiana Fever player acknowledged Reese’s offensive potential after having questioned some of her plays in the playoffs. Days later, the Atlanta star put on a historic performance in the WNBA Finals.
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever player acknowledged Reese’s offensive potential after having questioned some of her plays in the playoffs. Days later, the Atlanta star put on a historic performance in the WNBA Finals.
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham was very critical of Angel Reese during the WNBA semifinals, but she also acknowledged one of the qualities that could help the Atlanta Dream star grow the most: her ability to improve her outside shooting.

On her podcast, “No Hesitation,” the Indiana Fever player highlighted Reese’s progress and noted that she still has room to expand her offensive repertoire.

The assessment drew attention because this time, she focused on Reese’s work ethic, her defensive skills, and the progress she has shown from the three-point lin

Sophie Cunningham acknowledges Angel Reese’s improvement

Cunningham explained that opposing teams can still afford to give Reese space on the perimeter. “When you play against Atlanta, you’re willing to give up that shot. You can live with her making three-pointers,” she said on the podcast.

Her regular-season stats supported that strategy: Reese made 11 of her 57 three-point attempts, a 19.3% success rate. However, her performance improved during the playoffs. Before Game 2 of the Finals, she had made 5 of her 14 three-point attempts, for a 35.7% success rate.

The improvement did not go unnoticed by Cunningham, who also highlighted Reese’s defensive play and her rebounding prowess. “She’s a great, great defensive player,” he said before outlining what he sees as the next step for the Atlanta big woman: “Her offensive game is going to improve.”

The Indiana player also praised the support of Atlanta coach Karl Smesko and the confidence he’s giving Reese to continue developing her shot. If she manages to become a more consistent threat from the perimeter, opposing defenses will have less leeway to close out on her near the basket.

Angel Reese responded with a historic performance in the Finals

The progress Cunningham had noted was further demonstrated on Monday, October 19. Reese scored 30 points and grabbed 16 rebounds in the Atlanta Dream’s 79-65 victory over the Golden State Valkyries in Game 2 of the WNBA Finals. The result tied the series at 1-1.

The center was decisive on both ends of the court and finished with 10 made shots out of 16 attempts, along with three assists and two blocks. Atlanta improved significantly after halftime and secured its first-ever victory in the Finals , having lost its previous ten games at that stage.

And her performance against Golden State reinforced that point. Reese still has aspects of her game to develop, but her impact in Game 2 of the Finals made it clear why Atlanta relies on her as one of the central figures in their franchise’s future.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark's Nike Caitlin 1 ‘Halloween’ goes head-to-head with Angel Reese's special Reebok sneakers inspired by Reese's
articles.standfirst: The WNBA stars continue to go head-to-head, even away from the basketball court
articles.summary: The WNBA stars continue to go head-to-head, even away from the basketball court
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese are bringing their rivalry into the sneaker market, with Nike 's glow-in-the-dark Caitlin 1 “Halloween” colorway facing off against a Reese 's-inspired Reebok collaboration featuring the Atlanta Dream star. The releases give basketball fans two distinctive designs tied to the players' signature footwear and comes at an interesting time as Reese recently delivered a standout performance in the WNBA Finals , recording 30 points and 16 rebounds as Atlanta defeated the Golden State Valkyries in Game 2 to level the series at 1-1.

Her new footwear arrives as the Dream pursue the franchise's first championship and she continues to star after her transfer from the Chicago Sky to Atlanta , whilst the Indiana Fever ’s Clark is watching from home after being eliminated by the Las Vegas Aces earlier in the WNBA Playoffs . The 24-year-old guard’s seasonal Nike edition embraces Halloween with luminous details, whilst Reese 's latest Reebok sneakers draw inspiration from the familiar chocolate and peanut butter candy brand. Both models retain their basketball identity while using distinctive visual themes to attract fans beyond the court as Clark 's edition emphasizes luminous Halloween detailing, whereas Angel ’s collaboration builds its appeal around a recognizable confectionery brand.

How Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese's signature sneakers compare

The Caitlin 1 “Jinx” is scheduled to arrive Friday, October 23, as part of Nike Basketball ’s 10-model Halloween collection. Priced between $140 and $150 in adult sizing, the shoe uses a predominantly black palette with Ghost Green, Mint Foam and Racer Blue accents. The standout feature is its glow-in-the-dark finish, which extends across the outsole, upper accents and layered Swooshes. Cat-eye details appear inside the tongue, while the insoles feature an illustration of Clark wearing a witch’s mask, connecting the design to its Halloween theme. The “Jinx” name also has a personal connection, referencing a neighbor’s cat that frightened Clark during her childhood. Raised green “22” and “CC” details highlight her jersey number and initials, giving the seasonal design a direct link to the Fever star. Nike ’s launch follows strong early demand for the Caitlin 1 . The debut colorways arrived October 1 and nearly sold out within roughly two hours, with CNBC reporting that Nike described the release as the biggest women’s signature shoe launch in its history. Reese ’s new Reebok collaboration takes a different approach, using the candy brand’s signature brown, orange and yellow colors. The sneakers feature the Reese ’s chocolate brand logo on the tongue flap and arrive in a special orange shoebox, with prices set at $160 for unisex sizes and $130 for children. "The Reese's x Reebok Angel Reese 1 brings Angel's unapologetic style and dominant on-court energy to a bold collaborative colorway inspired by the iconic candy brand," Reebok said. "Rich chocolate and peanut butter tones collide with performance-driven design details built for today's versatile game. “They're a bold fusion of performance innovation and expressive design, built to match Angel's dynamic on-court dominance and culture-driving presence off it. Engineered to support Angel's relentless energy in the game and built to inspire and impress, these basketball shoes balance ethereal aesthetics with elite-level performance." The Caitlin 1 platform includes an Opticast upper, forefoot Air Zoom Turbo cushioning and Cushlon foam. The Halloween edition retains that underlying setup, with the glow-in-the-dark finish serving as a visual feature rather than evidence of any performance upgrade.
