articles.standfirst: Reese won Game 2 of the WNBA Finals but it may not be enough to topple Clark’s popularity
articles.summary: Reese won Game 2 of the WNBA Finals but it may not be enough to topple Clark’s popularity
articles.body:
Angel Reese 's rise with the Atlanta Dream has strengthened her case as one of the WNBA's biggest stars, but former NFL player Emmanuel Acho believes a championship alone won't make her the face of the league.

Caitlin Clark 's popularity remains central to that debate in Acho ’s view, despite Reese 's growing accomplishments, although the 24-year-old’s offensive development has drawn praise from Acho .

He acknowledged that her improved post game deserves recognition, while making clear that individual growth and winning a title don't automatically settle the question of who represents the league.

“Angel Reese has gotten significantly more offensively competent,” Acho said on Speakeasy. “And it’s undeniable… What Angel Reese is doing now: she has competent post moves that she’s committing to memory… That to me is worthy of praise…

“I’m gonna tell the world when you’re balling, and when you’re not, [there are] going to be conversations. But I don’t think a championship makes her the face.”

The discussion over the league's leading star has largely revolved around Clark and Las Vegas Aces forward A'ja Wilson since Clark and Reese entered the WNBA in 2024.

Clark's ability to attract viewers and fill arenas has strengthened her claim, while Wilson's three championships and five MVP awards offer a compelling case based on sustained excellence.

A screenshot shared on X in August added another dimension to the argument. A list of videos from the WNBA's official YouTube channel showed different view counts for game highlights published on the same day.

A video featuring Wilson and the Aces had 19,000 views, while one featuring Reese had 23,000. A highlight featuring Clark and the Indiana Fever attracted 180,000 views, although another Clark highlight at the top of the list had only 15,000.

The figures helped fuel the argument that Clark remains the league's biggest draw, even as Reese 's profile has grown.

Reese 's social media following has long made her a prominent figure, but her on-court progress has given her additional reasons to be taken seriously in discussions about the WNBA's future.

Reese increases her popularity

Clark ’s contributions to Team USA at the FIBA World Cup, where she played a major defensive role in the gold medal victory, further strengthened her standing.

Reese subsequently earned Defensive Player of the Year recognition, adding another major achievement to her growing resume.

Reese 's performances in the 2026 WNBA Finals have added weight to the discussion. She scored 27 points as the Atlanta Dream defeated the Golden State Valkyries 79-65 in Game 2 at Chase Center on Monday, tying the best-of-seven series at one game apiece.

Atlanta seized control after the teams were tied 40-40 early in the third quarter, producing a 29-8 run that created a 21-point advantage. Golden State struggled offensively, with Gabby Williams the only starter to reach double figures with 14 points.

The series moves to Atlanta for Game 3 on Wednesday, October 21, at 14:00 ET/17:00 PT.

articles.summary: Finals collision course: Golden State Valkyries host the Atlanta Dream at Chase Center
articles.body:
T he WNBA 2026 Finals are on fire , and they feature the most compelling matchup the season could offer: the Golden State Valkyries, the Western Conference's second seed, against the Atlanta Dream, the regular-season kings of the Eastern Conference.

Both arrived riding momentum that borders on the absurd — each team swept its semifinal series in three straight games — and both have unfinished business to settle at the top of the sport.

WNBA Finals Game 2: Results and more from the last game

An 18,064-strong sell-out crowd at Chase Center came hoping to see the Golden State Valkyries hold home court. Instead they watched Angel Reese bully the paint for 40 minutes, dragging the Atlanta Dream to a commanding 79-65 playoff victory in San Francisco.

The Valkyries matched Atlanta almost shot-for-shot from the field — both sides finished 21-of-61 and 21-of-62 respectively, both 37 per cent on twos, both knocking down seven three-pointers at under 30 per cent. On pure shooting, this was a dead heat. The game was decided everywhere else.

Atlanta hammered Golden State from the free-throw line, converting 30 of 35 attempts (85 per cent) to the hosts' 16 of 19. That 14-point gap at the stripe is, almost exactly, the final margin.

The Dream also won the rebounding battle 36-32, created more for one another with 17 assists to 10, and turned defence into offence with 14 steals to eight. Golden State coughed the ball up 18 times against Atlanta's 14.

articles.title: Angel Reese sends clear message to critics during the WNBA Finals: “We don't need Caitlin Clark”
articles.standfirst: The Dream star has delivered standout performances
articles.summary: The Dream star has delivered standout performances
articles.body:
The WNBA has spent much of the past three seasons navigating comparisons between Angel Reese and Caitlin Clark , but the league's latest television figures have provided a different perspective on its growing popularity.

Reese 's first appearance in the WNBA Finals attracted a record audience, with 2.1 million viewers watching the Atlanta Dream face the Golden State Valkyries on NBC and Peacock.

The broadcast peaked at three million viewers despite Atlanta's 68-64 defeat, making it the most-watched opening game of a WNBA Finals series.

Those figures represented an 11 percent increase over the previous season's Game 1 audience, prompting supporters to revisit arguments about Clark 's influence on women's basketball.

The record-breaking audience generated immediate reactions on social media, particularly among supporters who believe Reese hasn't received sufficient recognition for her influence.

"DON'T NEED CC! Iowa fans are in a coma over this," one fan wrote on X after the viewing figures emerged.

Another supporter argued that Reese's presence had contributed to the impressive audience.

"I thought people weren't watching. This is that Angel Reese effect. Love to see it," the fan commented.

Others questioned suggestions that the WNBA would struggle to maintain interest without Clark participating in its championship series.

However, the ratings alone cannot establish how many viewers tuned in specifically to watch Reese or whether Clark' s popularity influenced broader interest in the league.

Why Angel Reese attracts WNBA viewers

Former WNBA star Sheryl Swoopes had already offered a strong defense of Reese before the championship series began.

Appearing on The Draymond Green Show, Swoopes argued that the Atlanta forward attracts considerable attention from both supporters and critics.

"You should tune into the finals because of Angel Reese," Swoopes said. "She alone is worth the price of the ticket...

"Angel is gonna have people watching this because there's a large consortium of people who want to see her succeed; there's an even larger group of people who want to see her fail, and they're gonna watch to see her fail."

Reese 's move from the Chicago Sky to Atlanta in April has provided an opportunity to compete for a championship after two frustrating seasons in Chicago.

Reese delivers dominant performance

The attention surrounding Reese was followed by one of the most impressive performances of her professional career.

She scored 30 points and grabbed 16 rebounds in Atlanta's 79-65 Game 2 victory, helping the Dream level the championship series at 1-1.

The performance underlined Reese 's importance to an Atlanta team attempting to secure its first WNBA championship.

During the regular season, she averaged 16.4 points and 12.1 rebounds, establishing herself as one of the league's most productive interior players.

The series now shifts to Atlanta, where Reese will have another opportunity to influence the championship race.

While comparisons with Clark continue to dominate online discussions, Reese 's Finals performances and the record television audience have demonstrated the wider appeal of a league with multiple recognizable stars.

articles.title: Angel Reese beats Caitlin Clark to the WNBA Finals and Reebok’s candy collab drops before Clark’s Nike Halloween shoe
articles.standfirst: Reese’s Reese’s Pieces-inspired Angel Reese 1 arrived Oct. 20; Clark’s Nike Caitlin 1 “Jinx,” with glow-in-the-dark accents, is set to launch Oct. 23
articles.summary: Reese’s Reese’s Pieces-inspired Angel Reese 1 arrived Oct. 20; Clark’s Nike Caitlin 1 “Jinx,” with glow-in-the-dark accents, is set to launch Oct. 23
articles.body:
Angel Reese is still playing for a WNBA championship. Caitlin Clark’s season with the Indiana Fever ended in the first round. Now Reese has another early lead over her former college rival: her Reebok collaboration hit stores three days before Clark’s Halloween-themed Nike shoes are due out.

Reese’s new Reebok Angel Reese 1 “REESE’S” is built around the candy’s familiar orange, brown and yellow colors. The design also nods to Reese’s fans, many of whom call themselves the “Reese’s Pieces.” “We designed this colorway especially for my fans,” Reese said. The shoes went on sale Oct. 20 for $160. Reebok lists an Energy Return System underfoot and a molded TPU upper designed to provide stability and durability.

Clark’s Halloween Nikes bring the glow

Clark’s * Nike Caitlin 1 “Jinx” takes a darker route. The black shoe has Ghost Green accents that glow in the dark, giving her signature model a Halloween look .

Nike says the Caitlin 1 uses an Air Zoom Turbo unit with Cushlon foam and a lightweight Opticast upper. The “Jinx” colorway is set to release Oct. 23 for $150.

The designs turn expectations on their head: Clark’s shoe is the spooky, attention-grabbing one, while Reese’s gets the playful candy palette.

Reese’s collaboration also ties directly to her fans ; Clark’s Halloween design draws on the story of Jinx, a neighborhood cat that frightened her when she was young.

Their games offer a different kind of contrast. Clark averaged 22.3 points and 8.3 assists per game for Indiana this season , ranking among the WNBA’s top scorers and playmakers.

Angel averaged 16.4 points and a league-best 12.1 rebounds for Atlanta. She set a league record with 32 double-doubles and became the first Dream player to win Defensive Player of the Year.

The Fever’s season ended with a 94-83 loss to the Las Vegas Aces on Oct. 1. Reese and the Atlanta Dream, meanwhile, are preparing to host the Golden State Valkyries for Game 3 of the WNBA Finals on Wednesday.

The series is tied 1-1, and the game is scheduled for 8 p.m. ET on USA Network and CNBC, with streaming on Peacock.

articles.standfirst: Cunningham will become a free agent, and many teams will vie for her services because of her popularity
articles.summary: Cunningham will become a free agent, and many teams will vie for her services because of her popularity
articles.body:
As WNBA guard Sophie Cunningham enters a crucial offseason as a free agent after spending two productive seasons playing in Indiana, her profile across the sports world and pop culture landscape has surged to unprecedented heights.

Known for her fierce perimeter play and outspoken personality, the 30-year-old veteran has captured national headlines, earning praise from high-profile figures including President Donald Trump while sparking intense online discourse following her candid comments on biological women in sports.

On the court, Cunningham continued to serve as a reliable floor-spacing option off the bench throughout the 2026 campaign . Across 43 regular-season games, she logged 22.2 minutes per contest while averaging 7.9 points, 2.3 rebounds, and 1.2 assists , connecting on 46.0 percent of her field goals and 41.9 percent of her three-point attempts.

Cunningham Shuts Down Awkward Dating Question on Live Camera

Despite her impressive statistical contributions and growing cultural footprint, the high-profile free agent recently found herself navigating a cringeworthy moment when his podcast parter pressed her on her personal life.

During a viral appearance on her podcast , Cunningham was confronted with an intrusive question inquiring about her dating life, the question was "What was the worst first date you ever had?" and Cunningham answer that she don't remember the last time she had a date.

"People don't approach me, so I don't really go on dates." Would that be true? Or was she just evading the answer? At 30 years old, with her focus on her game and business, it's likely that she's not dating but hard to believe.

About her future in the WNBA last week Cunningham posted a viral social media clip dancing and lip-syncing to Rihanna and T.I.'s 2008 hit track "Live Your Life."

Radiating confidence, the WNBA star emphatically mouthed the iconic lines: "Got my mind on my money / and I'm not going away / So keep on getting your paper." The playful yet direct response sent a resounding message to fans and critics alike that external distractions will not derail her momentum.

As front offices prepare their pitch decks for 2027 WNBA free agency , Cunningham’s combination of elite perimeter shooting and unflappable swagger positions her as one of the most sought-after veterans on the open market.

articles.title: Police block Enes Kanter Freedom from entering WNBA Finals arena
articles.standfirst: Enes Kanter Freedom’s WNBA Finals appearance took an unexpected turn after security directed him to a private suite amid safety concerns.
articles.summary: Enes Kanter Freedom’s WNBA Finals appearance took an unexpected turn after security directed him to a private suite amid safety concerns.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Dream and State Farm Arena took special security measures to allow former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom to attend Game 3 of the WNBA Finals against the Golden State Valkyries, although he was required to watch the game from a private suite.

However, a video shared on social media showed Kanter attempting to enter the arena without much success, arguing that he had purchased a ticket for the game.

In the footage, Freedom can be seen accompanied by police officers while he is unable to enter the arena to watch the action.

Freedom had expressed concerns about his safety and contacted federal, state and local authorities, as well as the WNBA, the Dream and arena officials.

“Following consultations with the WNBA, Dream ownership, State Farm Arena leadership and security officials, we have directed Mr. Freedom to watch tonight’s game from a private luxury suite. This arrangement is intended to address his security concerns and help provide a safe and positive experience for him and other guests. The suite will have additional security and will be his designated viewing location for the game. State police have also assigned an officer to Mr. Freedom at his request.”

The suite will have additional security and will be Freedom’s designated viewing location for the game. State police also assigned an officer to accompany him at his request.

Enes Kanter Freedom returns to a WNBA game after Natasha Cloud controversy

Freedom explained that he was motivated to attend the game after hearing Golden State Valkyries star Gabby Williams say she would support a transgender athlete playing in the league.

“As you all know, this all started with an interview featuring Gabby Williams of the Golden State Valkyries, when she said, ‘I have no problem with trans athletes playing on my team or against my team,’” Freedom wrote in his post. “Her words gave me so much hope and motivation to come out as a woman and officially declare for the WNBA draft. I can’t wait to watch my favorite player, the woman who inspired me to become who I am today!”

Freedom and Royce Whit e, another former NBA player, have both declared for the WNBA draft , stating that they identify as women. However, a person familiar with the league’s decision told The Associated Press in August that neither player is eligible to enter the draft. WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert has since publicly confirmed that position.

On Wednesday, Freedom shared a photo of himself in Atlanta and also posted a copy of a letter from Engelbert responding to a question from Indiana Rep. Marlin A. Stutzman regarding the eligibility of transgender athletes to compete in the league.

“With respect to your questions regarding eligibility, only women are eligible to play in the WNBA, and the individuals you cite in your letter are both men,” Engelbert wrote, referring to Freedom and White.

Freedom responded by criticizing the league’s stance:

“Apparently the WNBA can still define what a WOMAN is, but they’re absolutely certain they know what a MAN is! How convenient!”

articles.standfirst: Angel Reese delivered another statement performance in the WNBA Finals, sparking the Atlanta Dream’s Game 3 victory over the Golden State Valkyries.
articles.summary: Angel Reese delivered another statement performance in the WNBA Finals, sparking the Atlanta Dream’s Game 3 victory over the Golden State Valkyries.
articles.body:
After her historic performance in Game 2 of the WNBA Finals , Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese once again showed she is unwilling to back down from anyone — and that her intensity remains one of the team’s greatest weapons.

Angel Reese lights up the WNBA Finals again

The Atlanta Dream hosted the Golden State Valkyries in Game 3 of the series a t State Farm Arena on Wednesday, looking to build on their momentum after tying the best-of-seven series with a win in Game 2.

Confidence was high for the home team. Early in the first quarter, Reese delivered a fiery moment when she turned toward the Valkyries’ bench after converting an and-1 opportunity against Aminata Gueye.

“You can’t f*** with me,” the fiery forward said after the play.

The 26-year-old was the star of Game 2, finishing with 30 points, 16 rebounds, three assists, and two blocks. That performance made her the youngest player in league history to record at least 30 points and 15 rebounds in a WNBA Finals game.

Her post on X following the victory also went viral, reflecting the strong support she has received throughout the Dream’s surprising playoff run.

After the Game 1 loss, Reese promised to become more aggressive offensively — and she delivered immediately. The reigning Defensive Player of the Year has been decisive on the court and has served as the team’s emotional leader through her energy and presence.

“This environment (Chase Center) is tough to play in. Shoutout to the fans. Shoutout to my team as well. We came here and fought. Game 1 was tough for us, but we turned the page, kept moving forward, and got back to being who we are,” Reese said.

Dream take 2-1 series lead

Reese finished with 21 points and 12 rebounds to help the Atlanta Dream defeat the Golden State Valkyries 97-71 on Wednesda y night and take a 2-1 lead in the WNBA Finals.

Rhyne Howard added 16 points, while Naz Hillmon scored 15 for the Dream , who will host Game 4 on Saturday.

It was Reese’s second straight dominant performance in the Finals after she posted 30 points and 16 rebounds in Game 2. She has now recorded a double-double in every game of the series.

articles.title: "Angel Reese is a game changer": The WNBA bows down to Reese after finals masterclass
articles.standfirst: With a historic third straight Finals double-double and Atlanta leading the series 2-1, Reese is turning her championship ambitions into a statement on the court
articles.summary: With a historic third straight Finals double-double and Atlanta leading the series 2-1, Reese is turning her championship ambitions into a statement on the court
articles.body:
Angel Reese is giving the Atlanta Dream exactly what they hoped for when they brought her into the fold: relentless rebounding, defensive intensity and performances that can change the direction of a championship series.

The 24-year-old forward delivered another outstanding display on Wednesday, recording 21 points, 12 rebounds, three assists and three steals as Atlanta overwhelmed the Golden State Valkyries 97-71 in Game 3 of the WNBA Finals.

Her performance helped the Dream seize a 2-1 series lead and put them halfway to the first championship in franchise history.

The WNBA quickly celebrated Reese's latest achievement on social media, posting the emphatic declaration: “ Angel Reese is a GAME CHANGER,” alongside her Game 3 numbers.

The league also highlighted her remarkable consistency throughout the series: “ Angel Reese turned up in front of the home crowd,” the WNBA stated. “She was consistent from start to finish recording 21 PTS, 12 REB, 3 AST, 3 STL & 2 3PM on 7-12 shooting! She’s averaging 21.7 PPG & 13.3 RPG through the #2026WNBAFinals and becomes the second player to reach those averages across any 3-game WNBA Finals span, the other being A’ja Wilson.”

The comparison with Las Vegas Aces superstar A'ja Wilson underlines the level Reese has reached during her first Finals appearance.

She has produced a double-double in all three games, becoming the first player in WNBA history to accomplish that feat across her first three Finals outings.

But Reese's impact goes beyond a collection of impressive numbers. Her response to Atlanta's opening loss has helped transform the momentum of the series, while her energy and willingness to take responsibility have become central to the Dream's championship push.

From a frustrating opener to a historic Finals run

Reese's Finals began with disappointment. Atlanta led for much of Game 1 but eventually fell 68-64, with Reese unable to score in the second half after a productive opening quarter.

Rather than blame Golden State's defense, Reese accepted responsibility for her lack of aggression. That response set the stage for a spectacular turnaround two days later.

In Game 2, she exploded for 30 points and 16 rebounds as Atlanta earned a 79-65 victory, securing the franchise's first-ever win in a WNBA Finals game.

She became the third player in Finals history to record at least 30 points and 15 rebounds in a single game, joining Jonquel Jones and Breanna Stewart .

Reese also made clear how much the opening defeat had bothered her. She said she felt she had let the team down by failing to contribute enough after halftime, including through her screening, hustle and rebounding.

The second game offered an immediate answer. Reese attacked the basket, controlled the glass and added a threat from beyond the arc.

Her three-point shooting has become an increasingly useful part of her game, and Atlanta remains unbeaten in contests in which she makes at least one three-pointer, with its record now at 15-0.

Game 3 showed that the improvement was no one-night occurrence. Reese again scored efficiently, made both of her three-point attempts and helped Atlanta establish control after Golden State briefly tied the game at 49-49 in the third quarter.

The Dream responded with an eight-point run, including four points from Reese, before closing the period with 12 of the final 14 points. Golden State never recovered.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham finds the perfect pair of “breasts” to match her style
articles.standfirst: The Indiana Fever free agent is letting the criticism roll off her back, one TikTok at a time
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever free agent is letting the criticism roll off her back, one TikTok at a time
articles.body:
S ophie Cunningham is taking the criticism surrounding her offseason in stride after her contract with the Indiana Fever came to an end . While many fans want to see her return to the team, others argue that re-signing her would create more problems than simply letting her walk away.

Rather than letting the public reaction get to her, Cunningham appears to be having fun with it. The WNBA star is once again making light of the attention surrounding her, this time posting a TikTok video in which she finds the perfect pair of breasts to match her style .

Sophie Cunningham turns criticism into content

In the video, Cunningham dances while holding two pieces of fried chicken near her chest , moving along to the TikTok audio she chose for her performance. She then takes things a step further, devouring both pieces in a matter of seconds.

The video fits the carefree approach she has shown throughout the offseason , as Cunningham continues to make her own fun despite the criticism surrounding her basketball career and public image.

Cunningham has a message for her critics

Cunningham has made it clear that she is no longer concerned about what people say about her , even as some critics argue that her controversies have become a bigger part of her story than her performance on the court. She does not believe she needs a stat sheet to justify her place in the WNBA, and her latest TikTok reflects that attitude.

She has previously explained that living for praise means having to deal with the hate that comes with it , a mindset she says has changed how she handles public opinion. Rather than taking every criticism seriously, she appears comfortable living in the moment and not letting other people's reactions dictate how she behaves.

More criticism may follow, but Cunningham continues to give people something to talk about. The attention surrounding her has become part of her public profile, and she seems more than willing to keep moving forward on her own terms.

articles.title: Paige Bueckers shows off her toned body at a pool party during the offseason
articles.standfirst: The Dallas Wings star is taking time to recharge after a frustrating end to WNBA season
articles.summary: The Dallas Wings star is taking time to recharge after a frustrating end to WNBA season
articles.body:
P aige Bueckers had a disappointing end to her WNBA season, falling short of her ultimate goal of competing for a championship . For a competitor of her caliber, winning a title is the next step, and the Dallas Wings star was clearly hoping to achieve more after a promising start to her professional career.

However, Bueckers appears to be putting that heartbreak behind her as she recharges for next season . A video shared on TikTok showed her enjoying a pool party in a bikini, revealing her toned physique and defined abs while soaking up the sun.

Paige Bueckers enjoys time away from basketball

The Wings star looked relaxed as she spent time with her friends by the pool, recording TikTok videos and enjoying the offseason. After the pressure of her WNBA campaign, Bueckers seemed focused on making the most of her time away from the court and catching some rays.

These days off could help her recharge before returning to the league next season. Bueckers established herself as a steady presence for Dallas from her very first professional game , showing that she could handle a significant role in the WNBA.

Bueckers faces the next step in her development

Now, the challenge will be turning the disappointment of a first-round playoff exit into motivation to reach another level when the biggest moments arrive. Bueckers has already shown that she can carry a heavy workload, but taking the next step will require her to become even more decisive when games are on the line .

The talent is there, and Bueckers has demonstrated that she can compete at a high level . The next challenge is developing the killer instinct needed to break through against the league’s toughest defenses . That is often what separates the best players from those who go on to become true stars.

articles.title: The Ultimate Hybrid? Why fans call Angel Reese ‘Shaq and Jokic's baby’
articles.standfirst: Angel Reese's spectacular no-look pass during the WNBA Finals has fans comparing her physical dominance and creative playmaking to NBA legends Shaquille O'Neal and Nikola Jokic
articles.summary: Angel Reese's spectacular no-look pass during the WNBA Finals has fans comparing her physical dominance and creative playmaking to NBA legends Shaquille O'Neal and Nikola Jokic
articles.body:
A ngel Reese has given basketball fans another reason to talk after producing a stunning no-look pass that nearly became one of the highlights of the 2026 WNBA Finals.

The Atlanta Dream forward caught an outlet pass that was drifting over her head, saved it from going out of bounds and immediately sent an over-the-head pass toward teammate Rhyne Howard .

Howard was fouled before she could finish the play, but Reese's improvisation had already captured the attention of viewers.

One social media user summed up the moment with a comparison that quickly caught on: "IT'S LIKE IF JOKIC AND SHAQ HAD A BABY".

The reference brings together two very different basketball superstars. Shaquille O'Neal was renowned for his overwhelming strength and dominance near the basket, while Nikola Jokic has become one of the NBA's most creative passing big men.

Reese's game is not identical to either legend's, but her combination of rebounding, physicality and improving court vision explains why fans are making the comparison.

The pass that had fans talking

The reaction to Reese's near-assist spread quickly across social media, with supporters imagining how memorable the sequence would have been had Howard converted the opportunity: "Would’ve been assist of the playoffs !! 😭"

Another fan praised Reese's overall influence on the league, writing: "She’s runs the league I’ve seen enough I’m sorry Aja you still the goat though".

Others were simply enjoying the show: "She Showing out 😭😭😭"

"The finals have activated Angel Prime," another said.

The excitement reflects Reese's growing reputation as a player who can influence games in several ways. She is an elite rebounder, a powerful presence inside and increasingly willing to create opportunities for her teammates.

Reese is backing up the hype in the Finals

The viral pass was not an isolated moment in an otherwise quiet performance. Reese has been central to Atlanta's push for a championship, producing three consecutive double-doubles to open the Finals.

After recording 14 points and 12 rebounds in Game 1, she erupted for 30 points and 16 rebounds as the Dream defeated the Golden State Valkyries 79-65 in Game 2.

She followed that performance with 21 points, 12 rebounds, three assists and three steals in Game 3, helping Atlanta secure a 97-71 victory and a 2-1 series lead.

Those numbers underline why the Shaq-Jokic comparison resonates. Like O'Neal, Reese can use her strength and positioning to control the paint. The passing sequence, meanwhile, showcased the creativity that fans associate with Jokic .

Of course, one highlight does not put Reese on the same level as two NBA greats. But it does demonstrate the range of skills she is bringing to the biggest stage of her young career.

With Atlanta now leading the best-of-seven series, Reese has a chance to turn her individual performances into something even more significant: a championship.

For fans, the no-look pass was a glimpse of her creativity. For the Dream, her rebounding, scoring and defensive energy could prove even more important as the Finals continue.

articles.title: Angel Reese reignites the debate with Caitlin Clark: Dan Patrick compares her to Moses Malone and fans are already talking about Giannis
articles.standfirst: Atlanta Dream star is having the best moment of her career in the WNBA Finals. Dan Patrick praised her toughness, but questioned her offensive repertoire, and social media responded with an even bigger comparison.
articles.summary: Atlanta Dream star is having the best moment of her career in the WNBA Finals. Dan Patrick praised her toughness, but questioned her offensive repertoire, and social media responded with an even bigger comparison.
articles.body:
The discussion between Angel Reese and Caitlin Clark seemed to have lost momentum as the season went on, but Reese's first WNBA Finals have once again put the two stars face to face. This time, Clark didn't even need to be on the court.

Journalist Dan Patrick reopened the debate by referring to Reese’s spectacular run with the Atlanta Dream and rejecting the idea that her results prove that she is already a better player than Clark . For Patrick, they are two completely different talents, although his analysis of Angel’s offensive game sparked an immediate reaction among fans by putting her on a par with Moses Malone.

The media rivalry between Angel Reese and Caitlin Clark is resurfacing even when one of them is not on the court. Reese is playing in her first WNBA Finals with the Atlanta Dream, and her performance has reignited a comparison that has followed both players for more than two years.

Dan Patrick sees Angel Reese as a new Moses Malone

Patrick has described Reese as a “relentless” player, that is, tireless , and found in Moses Malone a reference to explain her style.

The comparison is not focused so much on technique as on the way of competing. Malone built much of his dominance around rebounds, points from second chances, and his ability to impose himself physically near the rim.

That profile also defines a good part of Reese's game. The Atlanta star may not have the offensive repertoire of other great scorers, but her impact does not depend solely on shooting. She rebounds, attacks the rim, and keeps constant pressure on the opposing defense.

And in these Finals she is taking that formula to another level.

Reese delivers in the Finals and Atlanta takes the lead

After posting 30 points and 16 rebounds in the second game, Reese delivered again in the third matchup.

The player finished with 21 points, 12 rebounds, three assists and three steals, shooting 7 of 12 from the field, to help Atlanta defeat Golden State 97-71. The win put the Dream ahead 2-1 in the series.

In addition, Reese recorded a double-double for the third consecutive game in the Finals. At 24 years old, she became the youngest player in WNBA history to achieve three consecutive double-doubles in a championship series.

Social media takes the comparison all the way to Giannis

The comparison with Moses Malone opened another door on social media. Some fans began using the name of Giannis Antetokounmpo to describe Reese's evolution, especially because of her combination of size, physical power, attacking the rim, and ability to influence different aspects of the game.

That does not mean there is a direct comparison between the two players. For now, it is a reaction from fans to Reese's development and the way she is playing in the Finals.

What is evident, however, is that her game is generating a different conversation from that of her first months in the WNBA. It is no longer only about whether she can compete with Caitlin Clark in an individual discussion.

Reese now has an opportunity of her own: to lead Atlanta to its first WNBA championship. And after three games, the Dream are just two wins away from achieving it.

articles.title: Angel Reese ignites Atlanta's celebration and makes history in the WNBA Finals
articles.standfirst: The Dream star posted 21 points and 12 rebounds in the 97-71 rout of Golden State, recorded her third straight double-double in the Finals, and put Atlanta up 2-1 in the championship series.
articles.summary: The Dream star posted 21 points and 12 rebounds in the 97-71 rout of Golden State, recorded her third straight double-double in the Finals, and put Atlanta up 2-1 in the championship series.
articles.body:
Angel Reese was once again a central figure on the biggest stage in the WNBA. The Atlanta Dream star led her team with 21 points and 12 rebounds in the 97-71 victory over the Golden State Valkyries in Game 3 of the Finals, a result that put Atlanta ahead 2-1 in the best-of-seven series.

Reese also finished with three assists and three steals, shooting 7 of 12 from the field and a perfect 2 of 2 from three-point range. It was her second straight big game after the 30 points and 16 rebounds she recorded in Game 2.

Angel Reese makes history again

With this latest double-double, Reese became the youngest player in WNBA history to record three double-doubles in her first three Finals games . She also set the record as the youngest player to post at least 20 points and 10 rebounds in consecutive Finals games.

But the Dream's victory did not depend solely on its star. Rhyne Howard contributed 16 points and five steals, Naz Hillmon added 15, and Jordin Canada finished with 10 points and eight assists. Isobel Borlase chipped in another 12 points off the bench, and Atlanta ended up with five players in double figures.

The game definitively changed in the third quarter . Golden State managed to tie the score at 49, but Atlanta responded with an 8-0 run in which Reese scored four points. The Dream picked up the pace again in the final stretch of the period and closed the third with a 12-2 run to enter the last quarter with a 71-57 lead.

Atlanta turns State Farm Arena into a party

The atmosphere was also part of the triumph. The Dream played their first home games of the Finals at State Farm Arena, after Games 3 and 4 were moved from Gateway Center Arena, the team's usual venue, in order to accommodate a much larger crowd.

The decision paid off: 17,099 fans packed the venue for Game 3 and backed the Dream during a historic night.

After the game, Reese specifically highlighted the role of the fans and made it clear that Atlanta wants to recreate the atmosphere on Saturday.

“Our fans were there on every possession. I thought Ballhalla was loud, but Atlanta came out with everything. On Saturday, they have to do it again.”

Atlanta will host Golden State again on Saturday, October 24, in Game 4 of the Finals. The Dream is just two wins away from the first championship in its history , while Reese continues to raise her level at the most important moment of the season.

articles.title: Angel Reese enjoys the sellout in Atlanta: Why do some fans attribute it to Caitlin Clark?
articles.standfirst: Reese finished with 21 points and 12 rebounds in the 97-71 victory over the Golden State Valkyries, which gave the Dream a 2-1 lead in the series. The forward recorded her third consecutive double-double in these Finals after posting 30 points and 16 rebounds in the second game.
articles.summary: Reese finished with 21 points and 12 rebounds in the 97-71 victory over the Golden State Valkyries, which gave the Dream a 2-1 lead in the series. The forward recorded her third consecutive double-double in these Finals after posting 30 points and 16 rebounds in the second game.
articles.body:
Angel Reese and Atlanta Dream played in front of 17,099 spectators this Wednesday, October 21, at State Farm Arena, with tickets sold out for Game 3 of the WNBA Finals. The change of venue made it possible to welcome a much larger crowd than Gateway Center Arena, the team's usual home court, which has a capacity of about 3,500 people.

The sellout also sparked a discussion on social media. The Shadow League gathered comments from some Caitlin Clark supporters who attributed part of that turnout to the interest the Indiana player has generated around the competition. Those reactions questioned the prominence given to Reese, although they did not provide data on the reasons why attendees had bought their tickets.

Atlanta sellout fuels comparison between Angel Reese and Caitlin Clark

As MARCA already reported, Reese finished with 21 points and 12 rebounds in the 97-71 win over the Golden State Valkyries, which left the Dream with a 2-1 lead in the series. The forward recorded her third consecutive double-double in these Finals, after posting 30 points and 16 rebounds in the second game.

After the win, the player thanked the support she received from the stands. “Our fans were there for every possession,” she said before asking for that atmosphere to be repeated at the next home game: “On Saturday, they have to do it again”.

The discussion about her drawing power had begun before the game. On her program, Linda Cohn acknowledged Reese's popularity, but questioned whether prices listed on resale platforms were enough to equate her commercial impact with Clark's. She also noted that fans were buying tickets to watch the Dream compete for their first championship, with other stars such as Rhyne Howard, Jordin Canada, and Allisha Gray.

Among the reactions compiled by The Shadow League, one user wrote: “The Caitlin Clark effect works even when she doesn’t play”. Another added: “You can thank CC, Sophie and Lexie”, referring to Clark, Sophie Cunningham and Lexie Hull. The comments come from fans, not from statements by the Indiana players.

The crowd response at State Farm Arena did not begin with these Finals either. According to Front Office Sports, Atlanta played six regular-season games there and sold out five of them. For the title series, the entire arena was opened, unlike the first rounds of the playoffs, when mainly the lower bowl and a small section of the upper level were opened.

The fourth game will be played on Saturday, October 24, once again at State Farm Arena. Atlanta needs two more wins to capture the first championship in its history in a best-of-seven series.

articles.title: ESPN analyst gives Angel Reese ringing endorsement and nominates her for MVP: “She deserves her flowers and everyone’s respect”
articles.standfirst: The Atlanta forward has impressed Chiney Ogwumike with her dominant Finals performances
articles.summary: The Atlanta forward has impressed Chiney Ogwumike with her dominant Finals performances
articles.body:
Angel Reese has faced persistent questions about her offensive game throughout her professional career, but the Atlanta Dream forward is answering those critics when the stakes could hardly be higher.

With Atlanta two victories away from its first WNBA championship, Reese has emerged as one of the defining figures of the Finals, combining her familiar rebounding dominance with an increasingly confident scoring touch.

Her transformation has impressed ESPN analyst Chiney Ogwumike , who believes the 24-year-old deserves considerably more recognition for her development and influence on the Dream 's success.

Ogwumike went further than simply praising Reese 's performances, declaring that she would already select her as the championship series' Most Valuable Player.

Speaking on ESPN's First Take, Ogwumike highlighted Reese's production and the unexpected improvement in her perimeter shooting.

"She's my Finals MVP, no question about it," Ogwumike said. "And what she's been able to do has been truly impressive. She's averaging over 21 and 13 so far in the WNBA Finals.

"But more importantly, her team is 15-and-0 when she knocks down a three."

Reese has averaged 21.7 points and 13.3 rebounds through three Finals games, shooting 56.4 percent from the field and 75 percent from three-point range.

Those numbers represent a significant offensive improvement for a player who converted just 19.3 percent of her three-point attempts during the regular season.

Ogwumike credited Atlanta coach Karl Smesko with helping reshape Reese's shooting technique, providing another dimension to an offense that already possessed considerable talent.

"She has been the missing link for a team that has had talent," Ogwumike said. "And she now sets them over the edge."

Reese responds to Game 1 defeat

Reese 's influence became particularly apparent after Atlanta lost the opening game of the series, placing immediate pressure on the Dream to respond.

She delivered 30 points and 16 rebounds in Game 2, helping Atlanta secure a 79-65 victory before adding another 21 points and 12 rebounds in Game 3.

Those performances placed Reese alongside A'ja Wilson among players to record consecutive games with at least 20 points and 10 rebounds in the WNBA Finals.

"Whatever the team needed tonight, I was willing to do," Reese said after Game 2, reflecting the approach that has defined her postseason.

Atlanta Dream star receives recognition

Reese 's championship performances have built upon a regular season in which she averaged 12.1 rebounds and earned Defensive Player of the Year honors.

Her defensive presence, rebounding and improved scoring have helped transform Atlanta from a talented contender into a team with a genuine opportunity to win its first championship.

Ogwumike believes that development deserves recognition regardless of the criticism that has followed Reese throughout her career.

"And so, this is a unique era for the WNBA, and she deserves her flowers and everyone's respect," Ogwumike said.

The Finals MVP award remains undecided, but Reese has already strengthened her reputation considerably. With Game 4 approaching, another dominant performance would move Atlanta closer to the title and further reinforce Ogwumike 's endorsement.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark takes a breather as Angel Reese makes things tough for her and the entire WNBA
articles.standfirst: Angel Reese’s numbers with the Atlanta Dream are out of this world. The WNBA star is setting a nearly impossible standard for future generations to match.
articles.summary: Angel Reese’s numbers with the Atlanta Dream are out of this world. The WNBA star is setting a nearly impossible standard for future generations to match.
articles.body:
We never got to see Caitlin Clar k in the WNBA Finals , but Angel Reese has made sure the biggest stage still has a superstar putting on a show. The Atlanta Dream forward is delivering a historic performance, dominating the Finals and cementing her place alongside some of the greatest players in league history.

Reese once again delivered when it mattered most, leading the Dream to a dominant 97-71 victory over the Golden State Valkyries in Game 3 of the WNBA Finals on Wednesday night at State Farm Arena. The young star finished with 21 points, 12 rebounds, three assists and three steal s in 34 minutes, shooting 7-of-12 from the field .

The win gave Atlanta a 2-1 lead in the best-of-seven series and moved the franchise closer to what would be its first championship in team history.

According to ESPN Insights , Reese became the first player in WNBA history to record a double-double in each of her first three career Finals games . She also joined A’ja Wilson as the only players ever to record consecutive 20-point, 10-rebound performances in the same WNBA Finals series.

Reese’s dominance has been a constant throughout the series. In her Finals debut, she posted 14 points and 12 rebounds in the Game 1 loss, before exploding for 30 points and 16 rebounds in Game 2, leading the Dream to the first Finals victory in franchise history.

The Dream are two wins away from a championship

In Game 3, Reese showed another dimension of her skill set. The reigning Defensive Player of the Year surprised from beyond the arc, knocking down two three-pointers, a part of her game that has rarely been a focal point.

Her first three came late in the opening quarter and helped Atlanta build a 22-12 lead . Her second triple extended the advantage to 30-23 in the second quarter, and shortly after, she made a key defensive impact with a steal that led to a Rhyne Howard three-pointer .

According to the WNBA , the Dream remain undefeated this season — including the regular season and playoffs — whenever Reese makes at least one three-pointer.

Beyond the numbers, Reese continued to bring the intensity and confidence that have become part of her identity. After drawing a foul on a layup against Aminata Gueye , the Atlanta star celebrated in front of the Valkyries before sharing a chest bump with teammate Allisha Gray .

Atlanta once again showed its depth and balance. Rhyne Howard added 16 points, Naz Hillmon scored 15 and Isobel Borlase contributed 12 points off the bench. The Dream shot 49% from the field and turned Golden State’s 17 turnovers into 22 points.

For the Valkyries , Gabby Williams led the team with 15 points, but she needed 18 shots to get there. Cecilia Zandalasin i added 13 points, while Golden State struggled offensively, shooting just 35% from the field .

The Valkyries now face a critical moment and need a much stronger performance to avoid falling into a nearly impossible hole.

With the opportunity to capture the first championship in franchise history, the Atlanta Dream are only two wins away from the title and will look to take a commanding advantage when they host Game 4 on Saturday.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark’s Nike shoe set a record now Angel Reese and Reebok are making their move
articles.standfirst: Nike’s record-setting Caitlin Clark launch set the pace as Reebok responds
articles.summary: Nike’s record-setting Caitlin Clark launch set the pace as Reebok responds
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark’s first signature Nike shoe arrived with a launch the company called the biggest ever for a women’s signature sneaker. Now Angel Reese and Reebok are adding their own momentum , with a fresh collaboration that puts two of the WNBA’s most recognizable stars at the center of a growing footwear race.

The Caitlin 1 debuted in the United States on Oct. 1 in two colorways, “Caitlin Blue” and “Warning Code Yellow,” at $140. Nike CEO Elliott Hill said the launch reached 5,000 stores twice the average for a Nike basketball signature shoe. He also said Nike’s women’s signature basketball business grew nearly 500% from fiscal 2022 to fiscal 2026.

Nike’s scale meets Reebok’s comeback

Reebok has been building its own signature line around Reese. The original Angel Reese 1 sold out in all three launch colorways on Reebok’s website within hours in 2025. This week, the brand added another chapter with a Reese’s-inspired version, priced at $160 for adults. Reebok has not released comparable unit or revenue figures for either launch.

The latest Angel Reese 1, created with REESE’S, pairs its orange , brown and yellow candy-inspired look with performance features designed for the court. It has Reebok’s Energy Return System underfoot and a molded upper for stability and durability, plus co-branding on the tongue and sockliner.

The competition extends beyond Clark and Reese. Nike also has signature lines with Sabrina Ionescu and A’ja Wilson , while Puma’s WNBA signature star is Breanna Stewart. Reebok’s bet on Reese gives the brand a high-profile player as it continues to build its presence in basketball.

Caitlin Clark’s next Nike release to watch is the Caitlin 1 “Jinx,” a Halloween colorway with a black upper and glow-in-the-dark green accents. Nike’s Canadian SNKRS page lists it for Oct. 31, while U.S. sneaker reports point to an Oct. 30 release for $150. Fans should check Nike, SNKRS and Clark’s official channels for updates on their local release.

There are signs that more fans are buying women’s basketball shoes. StockX reported that sales of WNBA signature sneakers on its marketplace rose 938% from 2023 to 2024. That figure tracks activity on a resale platform, however, and doesn’t show how many pairs the brands sold through stores.

The real test for both brands will be whether the early excitement turns into sustained sales and whether they share enough numbers to show which one is gaining ground in the growing market for WNBA stars’ signature sneakers.

articles.title: “Not in this lifetime”: Angel Reese responds to a man who proposed to her
articles.standfirst: An Atlanta Dream fan surprised the WNBA star with an unexpected request, and she responded on social media.
articles.summary: An Atlanta Dream fan surprised the WNBA star with an unexpected request, and she responded on social media.
articles.body:
A ngel Reese was one of the stars of the Atlanta Dream’s victory over the Golden State Valkyries in Game 3 of the WNBA Finals. The Georgia team won 97-71 on Wednesday, October 21, taking a 2-1 lead in the championship series.

Reese contributed 21 points to the win, but another moment during the game also caught people’s attention. Amid the excitement of the Finals, the basketball star received a marriage proposal .

The sign a fan used to surprise Angel Reese

The TikTok content creator known as @tikibeen1 showed up to the game wearing a suit and tie and carrying a huge sign addressed to Reese. His message got straight to the point: “Angel Will You Marry Me?”

The proposal turned the fan into the center of a scene that soon began circulating on social media. The video eventually reached Angel Reese, who left a comment that gave the story an unexpected twist.

“Not in this lifetime but i have some fine friendsssss,” she wrote.

With that response, Reese turned down the proposal without losing her sense of humor, even offering the hopeful admirer an alternative.

What happened to Angel Reese’s boyfriend, Wendell Carter Jr.?

Reese’s response also sparked interest in her love life, particularly one question: Is she still in a relationship with Wendell Carter Jr., a center for the NBA’s Orlando Magic?

Based on the information publicly available, the two have been linked romantically, although they have chosen to keep much of their relationship private rather than constantly putting it in the spotlight .

Beyond the attention surrounding this moment, Reese and her teammates are preparing for Game 4 of the Finals against the Golden State Valkyries, scheduled for Saturday, October 24, at 7 p.m. ET .

A win would give Atlanta a 3-1 lead in the series and put the team just one victory away from claiming the WNBA championship.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark is keeping an eye on Stephanie White after a resignation and firing from Indiana Fever
articles.standfirst: Indiana has undergone a major leadership shake-up after a disappointing playoff exit, with Kelly Krauskopf stepping down and general manager Amber Cox losing her job
articles.summary: Indiana has undergone a major leadership shake-up after a disappointing playoff exit, with Kelly Krauskopf stepping down and general manager Amber Cox losing her job
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever 's offseason has begun with a dramatic change behind the scenes, raising fresh questions about the franchise's direction and the people responsible for building a championship contender around Caitlin Clark .

On Friday, October 23, the Fever confirmed that president Kelly Krauskopf would step down, before general manager Amber Cox was fired just hours later.

The decisions mark a significant shift for an organization that entered the 2026 WNBA season hoping to turn its growing talent and popularity into a serious title challenge.

For now, head coach Stephanie White is expected to retain her position, according to sources cited by ESPN.

That leaves her facing another season with considerable expectations, while Clark and her teammates await clarity over the leadership structure that will guide their next campaign.

The timing is notable. Indiana finished the regular season with a 28-16 record, setting a new franchise high for wins, but ended up as the sixth seed in the playoffs for the third consecutive season.

The Fever then lost their first-round series against the Las Vegas Aces , falling short of the ambitions that had surrounded the team.

Cox , who joined Indiana in 2024 as general manager and chief operating officer, oversaw a combined 52-36 regular-season record across her two campaigns. Mel Raines , president and CEO of Pacers Sports & Entertainment, acknowledged her contribution in a statement.

"Through her two seasons with the Fever, Amber has helped us navigate the seismic growth of both the WNBA and our franchise," Mel Raines , president and CEO of PS&E, said in a statement. "We're grateful for her contributions and wish her the very best moving forward."

Why Stephanie White's future matters to Caitlin Clark

Although White is expected to stay, the leadership changes leave the coach facing important questions about how Indiana can turn regular-season success into a deeper postseason run.

The Fever's offensive production was one of the biggest positives of 2026. Indiana averaged 96 points per game, setting a WNBA single-season scoring record, while Clark , Kelsey Mitchell and Aliyah Boston all earned All-Star recognition.

Mitchell and Clark finished second and third in regular-season scoring, respectively, with Clark also ranking second in assists.

However, the team's defensive weaknesses proved costly. Indiana allowed 90.4 points per game during the regular season, and its inability to consistently stop opponents became a concern as the playoffs approached.

The Aces ultimately ended the Fever's campaign with a 94-83 victory in Game 3 of their first-round series.

That contrast between offensive firepower and defensive inconsistency will be central to the offseason.

White must find ways to get more out of the roster, but the new front-office leadership will also have responsibility for identifying the players needed to address the team's weaknesses.

The question of who will replace Cox is therefore especially important. Indiana needs a general manager capable of building a balanced roster around Clark , rather than relying exclusively on the team's offensive strengths.

Another major issue concerns Mitchell . The veteran guard is an unrestricted free agent after an outstanding season, and her decision could have a significant impact on Indiana's plans.

Retaining her would preserve one of the league's most productive scoring partnerships with Clark ; losing her would force the Fever to find another way to replace that output.

Clark's own future is also part of the wider picture, with Indiana facing important contract decisions as it builds around its franchise star. The changes at executive level will influence how those negotiations and roster priorities are handled.

The Fever have made clear through their actions that the current direction has not delivered the results they wanted. But the departures of Krauskopf and Cox do not automatically resolve the problems that surfaced on the court.

For Clark , the immediate focus will be on returning to contention with a stronger supporting cast. For White , the challenge is to demonstrate that she can guide the team beyond another early playoff exit.

And for Indiana's next general manager, the task will be to build a roster capable of matching the franchise's ambitions.

The Fever have the star power and offensive production to compete with the league's best. Their next decisions will determine whether that potential can finally translate into a sustained postseason breakthrough.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark doesn't want to know anything about the WNBA finals or Angel Reese while she watches a different kind of basketball
articles.standfirst: The Indiana Fever star turned her attention to the NBA as she attended the Pacers’ home opener
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever star turned her attention to the NBA as she attended the Pacers’ home opener
articles.body:
C aitlin Clark was back courtside in Indianapolis on Friday night, but this time the Indiana Fever superstar was watching a different basketball team take center stage.

Clark attended the Indiana Pacers ’ home opener against the Dallas Mavericks at Gainbridge Fieldhouse, showing her support for Tyrese Haliburton as he played his first home game since returning from a devastating Achilles injury.

Her appearance came while the WNBA Finals continued without the Fever , who were eliminated in the first round of the playoffs.

With the championship series between the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries generating plenty of attention, Clark’s decision to spend the evening watching the NBA offered a reminder that her basketball interests extend beyond her own league.

There is no indication that Clark was deliberately avoiding news about the Finals or Angel Reese . However, her appearance at the Pacers game put her in the spotlight at a time when Reese is competing for a WNBA championship with Atlanta.

Clark and Haliburton have developed a close friendship through their shared connection to Indiana basketball.

The Fever guard has supported the Pacers star during his recovery, while Haliburton has also made appearances at Fever games, highlighting the relationship between the state's two professional basketball franchises.

The occasion was particularly meaningful for Haliburton , whose return to the court had been one of the major talking points surrounding the start of the NBA season.

Clark supports Haliburton as the Pacers begin a new chapter

Haliburton had been sidelined since tearing his right Achilles tendon during Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals against the Oklahoma City Thunder.

The injury came at a devastating moment for Indiana, which had reached the deciding game of the championship series before losing its star guard.

He subsequently missed the entire 2025-26 campaign while recovering, leaving the Pacers without one of their most important players.

His competitive return arrived on Wednesday, when Indiana opened its season against the New Orleans Pelicans .

Haliburton delivered an impressive performance, scoring 23 points and recording 12 assists in a dramatic 123-120 victory. He also played a decisive role in the closing stages, helping the Pacers secure the win.

Friday's game therefore represented another milestone in his comeback, marking his first appearance at Gainbridge Fieldhouse since the injury that ended his previous season.

Clark's presence showed her support for a player who has experienced the emotional and physical challenges of a lengthy rehabilitation.

Haliburton had previously attended a Fever game against the Phoenix Mercury on June 22, 2026, when he even helped retrieve a basketball that had become stuck behind the backboard.

That moment illustrated how the two Indiana stars have embraced their roles as representatives of the state's basketball community.

For Clark, attending the Pacers game also provided an opportunity to enjoy the sport away from the pressures of her own season. The Fever had already completed their campaign, giving her time to follow the NBA as Haliburton resumed his career.

The evening did not, however, end with a victory for the home team. Dallas defeated Indiana 121-105, spoiling the Pacers' home opener despite the excitement surrounding Haliburton's return.

Angel Reese and the WNBA Finals continue without Clark

While Clark watched from Indianapolis, Reese was helping Atlanta pursue the first championship in franchise history.

The Dream entered the Finals against the Golden State Valkyries after sweeping the New York Liberty in the semifinals. Reese had been a major contributor to Atlanta's playoff run, establishing herself as one of the team's leading performers during a successful first season with the franchise.

The Finals have already produced several compelling performances. Golden State won the opening game 68-64, but Atlanta responded with a 79-65 victory in Game 2, with Reese recording 30 points and 16 rebounds.

The Dream then won Game 3 by a score of 97-71, taking a 2-1 series lead into Saturday's fourth matchup.

Reese's involvement in the championship series inevitably brings renewed attention to her long-running public rivalry with Clark , which dates back to their college basketball days.

Their matchups have become major talking points among fans, with discussions about their respective performances often extending well beyond the court.

Nevertheless, Clark's attendance at an NBA game should not automatically be interpreted as a statement about Reese or the Finals.

The Fever star was there to support Haliburton during an important moment in his comeback, and the two players have consistently demonstrated mutual support through their connection to Indiana basketball.

With Clark's offseason underway and the WNBA championship still to be decided, the two storylines are unfolding separately.

For one evening, the focus was on Haliburton's return and the Pacers' attempt to start their new campaign strongly, rather than on the Finals race in the WNBA.

articles.title: Angel Reese’s simple striped look shows off her legs, but her Game 4 walk is pure star power
articles.standfirst: Reese arrives in a fitted, wine-and-rose striped two-piece and heels, carrying herself with a calm confidence
articles.summary: Reese arrives in a fitted, wine-and-rose striped two-piece and heels, carrying herself with a calm confidence
articles.body:
A ngel Reese’s outfit is more understated than some of the looks she has worn before: a matching two-piece set with thin vertical stripes in reddish and pink tones, a short skirt and heels. But as she walks through the arena hallway, the look becomes secondary to the way she carries herself. Her stride is smooth and unhurried; she seems happy, relaxed and focused.

There is no need for an extravagant entrance. Reese’s height, heels and easy cadence make her presence impossible to miss . She looks completely at home in the Finals spotlight and she arrives with Atlanta just two wins away from its first WNBA championship.

Angel Reese has made every Finals game count

Reese is coming off a 21-point, 12-rebound double-double in Atlanta’s 97-71 win over the Golden State Valkyries in Game 3. She has recorded a double-double in all three games of the Finals: 14 points and 12 rebounds in the opener, 30 points and 16 rebounds in Game 2, and another 21-and-12 performance on Wednesday. She is the youngest player to record double-doubles in three consecutive WNBA Finals games.

Her performances have helped Atlanta turn the series around. The Dream lost the opener, 68-64, but answered with a 79-65 win in Game 2 the first Finals victory in franchise history. They followed it with a 26-point blowout to take a 2-1 lead. The latest win was a team effort, with Rhyne Howard, Naz Hillmon, Isobel Borlase and Jordin Canada joining Reese in double figures.

Atlanta has also taken over the third quarter, outscoring Golden State 63-35 in that period across the first three games. In Game 3, the score was tied at 49 before the Dream pulled away. That surge, along with Reese’s work inside, has made it harder for the Valkyries to find their footing.

The Dream reached the Finals for the first time since 2013 after sweeping the Washington Mystics and New York Liberty. Now they have a chance to take a 3-1 lead in the best-of-seven series. A win would leave Atlanta one victory from the first title in franchise history; a Valkyries win would tie the series and shift the pressure back to the Dream.

Game 4 tips off Saturday at 1 p.m. ET at State Farm Arena, with coverage on NBC and Peacock. Reese’s walk into the arena is composed and carefree, but the opportunity in front of her is enormous: another win would bring Atlanta to the edge of the championship it has been chasing for years.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham becomes Angel Reese’s best ally in shifting the dynamic for Atlanta in the WNBA Finals
articles.standfirst: Sophie Cunningham weighs in on Angel Reese’s body language after her explosive Finals performance
articles.summary: Sophie Cunningham weighs in on Angel Reese’s body language after her explosive Finals performance
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham has shared a different perspective on Angel Reese’s emotional reaction during the WNBA Finals, suggesting the Atlanta Dream star’s frustration may have helped her team recognize what needed to change.

Reese attracted attention in Game 2 against the Golden State Valkyries after repeatedly calling for the ball in the post.

When teammates chose another option, she responded with animated gestures, sparking debate about her body language.

However, Cunningham believes the moment carried a message Atlanta needed to hear.

Speaking on her No Hesitation podcast, the Indiana Fever guard admitted Reese could have handled the situation better.

“Do I like the body language? Do I think that it could have been better? Absolutely,” said Cunningham . “And I think if she watches this back, I think she could have said the same thing.

“But three, sometimes you gotta do it. If your team’s not getting you the damn ball, then if you see one of your star players getting frustrated and getting pissed off, then it’s like, ‘Oh, they’re not messing around.

“We need to get her the damn ball.’ I think the coaching staff saw it; I think everyone on the bench saw it; her teammates felt the energy; and she did what she needed to do in order to put yet another game on her back.”

In Game 2, Reese had been working to establish position near the basket, but the ball went elsewhere. Her frustration quickly became a talking point, but talk quickly shifted back to her performance.

Reese finished with 30 points and 16 rebounds, shooting 10-for-16 from the field as Atlanta won 79-65 to tie the series. Her presence in the paint gave the Dream a boost and showed how influential she could be when involved consistently.

Reese’s response has changed Atlanta’s championship push

Reese carried that momentum into Game 3, helping Atlanta defeat Golden State 97-71. She recorded 21 points and 12 rebounds, giving the Dream a 2-1 series advantage and putting them within two wins of the championship.

The performance extended her run of consecutive Finals double-doubles, underscoring her impact on the biggest stage.

Head coach Karl Smesko has praised Reese’s development, highlighting her determination to improve throughout the season.

“She very well might be the most improved player from the beginning of the season to right now,” Smesko said.

Cunningham’s defense of Reese highlights the difference between showing frustration and allowing it to damage team chemistry. While expressive body language can invite criticism, it can also signal that a team needs to adjust.

articles.body:
The Golden State Valkyries defeated the Atlanta Dream (62-67) in the fourth game of the WNBA Finals played this Saturday, thanks to their stars Gabby Williams and Ceci Zandalasini returning to their best form ( 17 and 10 points respectively ) and tying the series for the championship ring (2-2).

The California team responded to the pressure after suffering two heavy defeats in a row, in a game in which they gave the home side no chance at any point, as they lost their first home game in the "playoffs" this season.

The Valkyries' strong defense on Angel Reese did not allow her to shine as she had in previous games, and she ended up with a poor 2/12 from the field.

After suffering their worst defeat of the season in Game 3 of the Finals (-26 points) , coach Natalie Nakase made two changes to Golden State's starting lineup, bringing in Tiff Hayes and Kaila Charles in search of greater offensive efficiency, leaving Italian player Zandalasini on the bench.

However, the plan did not work because the start followed the pattern of the last few matchups: no accuracy for the Californians and the Dream came out firing.

After a timeout by Nakase midway through the first half, and above all with the introduction of Cecilia Zandalasini onto the court, the Valkyries' energy changed on defense (with four consecutive steals and holding star Reese to 0 points in the first quarter) and, on offense, with a 12-0 run.

The intensity increased in the second period, and Golden State's two biggest stars showed up when their team needed them most.

"Ceci," with a nice drive through the middle, added a 2+1, which, together with the contribution of forward Gabby Williams (with seven almost consecutive points), gave the visitors their biggest lead on the scoreboard up to that point (+16).

Atlanta got a taste of its own medicine. It is the team that steals the most balls per game in the American league, but in the first half its 14 turnovers. doomed it.

In the restart, the Dream looked more like the energetic team that had come in on a two-game winning streak to rally in the series. A wing three-pointer by Australian Borlase cut the deficit to just 6 points (40-46).

But the "Violets" showed character and responded every time Atlanta got closer on the scoreboard to keep their distance.

In the final minutes, with the home side pouring forward urged on by their crowd, Tiff Hayes put the team on her back with productive drives to the basket, and a long-range three-pointer by Burton gave Golden State some breathing room (55-64 with 4:19 remaining).

The excitement lasted until the end. Rhyne Howard answered with an and-one to Veronica Burton's fade-away with 28 seconds remaining and Atlanta trailing by four , but two consecutive missed three-pointers by the home team sealed the victory for the Valkyries .

Next Monday they will return to San Francisco for the fifth game, which will be played at the Valhalla arena to break the tie in a finals series that will be decided in a best-of-seven format.

articles.title: A warning regarding what could happen with the Indiana Fever: "Keep Caitlin Clark happy or she's gone"
articles.standfirst: Caitlin Clark’s future in Indiana comes under scrutiny after Fever part ways with two top executives
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark’s future in Indiana comes under scrutiny after Fever part ways with two top executives
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever’s recent front-office shake-up has raised fresh questions about Caitlin Clark’s future, with former college basketball player and WNBA analyst Rachel DeMita warning that the franchise must give its superstar compelling reasons to stay.

Clark recently reaffirmed her commitment to Indiana, stating, “No matter what, I’m going to be here.” However, DeMita believes that loyalty shouldn’t prevent the star guard from exploring other opportunities if the organization fails to help her reach her full potential.

“Here’s the truth of the matter, it’s really something like keep Caitlin happy or she’s gone,” DeMita said on her Courtside Club podcast.

“I’m going to use Angel Reese as the example because I’ve said it many times. I think Angel leaving Chicago was the best thing that she could have done for her career. Caitlin can also do that, and Caitlin Clark should do that if she likes.”

Her warning comes as Indiana faces significant organizational changes following a disappointing postseason campaign.

Fever face crucial decisions after front-office shake-up

On Friday, October 23, team president Kelly Krauskopf announced her departure from the organization. Hours later, the Fever confirmed that general manager and chief operating officer Amber Cox had also been dismissed, leaving two senior leadership positions in transition.

The developments have intensified scrutiny of Indiana’s direction after the team finished sixth in the standings and suffered a first-round playoff elimination against the Las Vegas Aces.

The back-to-back departures have also fueled speculation about whether further changes could follow.

However, reports from USA TODAY’s Meghan L. Hall indicate that head coach Stephanie White is expected to retain her position for the 2027 season.

White has faced considerable attention during her second stint with Indiana, particularly because of the expectations surrounding Clark and the franchise.

Although the Fever made the playoffs in consecutive seasons under her leadership, their latest early exit has raised questions about what must change for the team to become a genuine championship contender.

Clark , meanwhile, delivered an impressive 2026 campaign, averaging a career-high 22.3 points, 8.3 assists, four rebounds and 1.1 steals per game. Despite those numbers, Indiana's postseason disappointment highlighted the work still required to turn individual performances into sustained playoff success.

DeMita believes the Fever must recognize how valuable Clark is to their future. Improving the supporting roster, establishing a clearer offensive system and strengthening the front office could all help create an environment in which the young superstar can thrive.

Reese’s experience offers a useful comparison. After two seasons with Chicago, she moved to Atlanta, illustrating how changing teams can provide fresh opportunities. Nevertheless, Clark hasn’t announced any intention to leave Indiana.

The leadership vacancies give the Fever an opportunity to reassess their basketball operations and build a stronger foundation around their core players. Finding executives capable of attracting talent and assembling a championship-caliber roster will be particularly important.

Clark has publicly expressed her commitment, and White is expected to remain head coach. Whether that stability continues will depend on how effectively Indiana addresses its shortcomings.

articles.title: Angel Reese admits her mistake in WNBA Finals Game 4: a performance to forget
articles.standfirst: Reese finished with eight points and nine rebounds, a far cry from the dominance she showed in the previous two games
articles.summary: Reese finished with eight points and nine rebounds, a far cry from the dominance she showed in the previous two games
articles.body:
A ngel Reese took responsibility and explained why she couldn’t find her rhythm when Atlanta needed her most. After dominating Games 2 and 3, the Dream star had an unusually difficult night against Golden State, scoring just eight points and grabbing nine rebounds in a 67-62 loss that tied the WNBA Finals at 2-2.

After the game, Reese acknowledged what went wrong around the basket. “I think I rushed a lot of my shots and I didn’t take my time and finish around the basket like I’ve been doing in the last three games. It happens,” she said at the press conference, looking visibly frustrated.

Golden State contained Angel Reese and tied the series

The Valkyries’ defense made every possession tougher. Golden State changed its starting lineup and stuck to its game plan, sending more defenders to cut Reese off. She finished 2-for-12 from the field, didn’t score in the first quarter and had five turnovers and three fouls by halftime.

Atlanta’s mistakes also helped create the gap. The Valkyries controlled the turnover battle in the first half, forcing 16 while committing just four and taking a 16-point lead into the break. The Dream fought back after halftime, but couldn’t complete the comeback.

Rhyne Howard led Atlanta with 19 points, while Isobel Borlase and Jordin Canada added 10 apiece. For Golden State, Gabby Williams finished with 17 points; Tiffany Hayes and Veronica Burton scored 13 each, and Kiah Stokes grabbed 16 rebounds.

The 67-62 win evened the WNBA Finals at 2-2, keeping Atlanta from moving within one victory of the championship. Game 5 is set for Monday, Oct. 26, in San Francisco at 8 p.m. ET.
