articles.title: Angel Reese’s big defensive moment isn’t enough as WNBA Finals shift again
articles.standfirst: The All-Star celebrated the block before turning toward her teammates, visibly energized by the stop
articles.summary: The All-Star celebrated the block before turning toward her teammates, visibly energized by the stop
articles.body:
A ngel Reese’s defensive intensity gave the Atlanta Dream a spark in Game 4 of the WNBA Finals , but it was not enough to prevent a 67-62 loss to the Golden State Valkyries, leaving the championship series tied 2-2. Reese finished with eight points, nine rebounds, three assists, one steal and three blocks. Her rejection of French star Gabby Williams in the first quarter became one of the game’s defining moments, showcasing the defensive presence and emotion that have helped fuel Atlanta’s Finals run.

The play also prompted a pointed observation from the NBC Sports broadcast. "You see the passion, you see the energy. That’s the difference in mentality for Atlanta,” the commentator said.

But by the final buzzer, Golden State had answered Atlanta’s recent surge with a crucial victory, ensuring the series would head into its next game level rather than leaving the Valkyries one loss away from elimination.

Reese’s defense makes an impression

With 2:28 remaining in the first quarter and Golden State leading 11-7, Williams brought the ball toward the basket with Reese tracking her closely. As Williams attempted to evade the Dream forward and finish at the rim, Reese swatted the shot away before it could reach the basket.

Reese celebrated the block before turning toward her teammates, visibly energized by the defensive stop.

The sequence reflected the approach she has brought to the series since Atlanta’s Game 1 defeat. After going scoreless in the second half of the opener, Reese said she needed to be more aggressive. The Dream subsequently responded with two victories to take a 2-1 lead.

In Game 4, Reese again made her presence felt defensively, recording three blocks and pulling down nine rebounds. Her eight points, however, came in a game where Atlanta struggled to generate enough offense to secure the win.

The defeat also complicated the Finals MVP conversation. Reese’s all-around contributions have made her one of the central figures in Atlanta’s run, but Golden State’s response means the series remains wide open.

Valkyries respond when the pressure rises

Golden State entered the Finals with one of the league’s strongest defensive identities, having posted a 99.3 defensive rating during the regular season. Gabby Williams earned All-Defensive First Team honors, while Kiah Stokes and Veronica Burton were named to the Second Team.

That reputation came under pressure when Atlanta scored 97 points in Game 3, setting a Dream franchise record for points in a Finals game. The Valkyries, who had swept the defending champion Las Vegas Aces in the semifinals, now have a chance to build on their Game 4 performance.

Their 67-62 win demonstrated that they could slow Atlanta down after the Dream had found their rhythm offensively. The low-scoring result also underscored how dramatically the matchup shifted from Game 3. This time, Atlanta could not translate its energy into enough points to maintain control of the series.

The 67-62 result changes the pressure on both teams. Atlanta missed its opportunity to take a 3-1 lead, while Golden State avoided falling into a difficult position heading into the next game. The challenge for Angel Reese is to maintain her defensive impact while helping the Dream find more scoring against a Valkyries team that rediscovered its defensive edge.

articles.title: Angel Reese's Game 4 performance came with a silver lining despite brutal loss
articles.standfirst: The Atlanta Dream couldn't get anything going offensively against the Golden State Valkyries, and the WNBA Finals are now tied at 2-2.
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream couldn't get anything going offensively against the Golden State Valkyries, and the WNBA Finals are now tied at 2-2.
articles.body:
The arrow was pointing way up for the Atlanta Dream heading into Saturday. With a 2-1 series lead and playing at home, the Dream could have come within one win of a championship with a victory at State Farm Arena in Atlanta, Georgia on Saturday.

The shots simply weren't falling for Atlanta, though. A 33% team field goal percentage , paired with nine missed free throws , kept the Dream from getting a crucial win. The Golden State Valkyries won 67-62 and have now tied the series at 2-2 with home court advantage in their favor.

There were many culprits for Atlanta's offensive struggles, but Angel Reese has taken the brunt of the blame. Reese shot a measly 2-of-12 from the field, while also committing six turnovers . Despite many fans online lighting into Reese for her performance, there was at least a silver lining for her: She actually led the team in plus-minus .

Angel Reese and Alisha Gray led the team with a +1 plus-minus in Dream's Game 4 loss to Valkyries

Reese was a +1 for the game, as was Alisha Gray . They led the Dream, while the other three starters were all negative: Jordin Canada with -1 , Naz Hilllmon with -4 , and Rhyne Howard with -6 . The bench was particularly detrimental, as DeWanna Bonner was -9 and Isobel Borlase was -7 . No one else played more than a minute.

Even though she struggled to score and keep possession throughout the game, Reese still contributed in other ways like she always does . She grabbed nine rebounds , handed out three assists , blocked three shots , and added one steal . That was enough to make her impact an overall positive one in Game 4.

The Dream only lost by five points despite a lot of things going wrong on Saturday. But if they continue to struggle to score, they might not be able to get back into the series before it's too late.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark fans urge her to follow Angel Reese’s path to the WNBA Finals as coach Stephanie White may stay
articles.standfirst: Indiana’s front-office shake-up brought major changes
articles.summary: Indiana’s front-office shake-up brought major changes
articles.body:
C aitlin Clark is entering her third WNBA season as one of the league’s biggest stars and most recognizable faces. But while Angel Reese is playing in the WNBA Finals with the Atlanta Dream , Clark still hasn’t reached the championship series with the Indiana Fever. That contrast has some fans asking whether she should follow Reese’s lead and find a new home.

The conversation grew louder as Indiana began reshaping its front office. Some Fever fans had hoped the changes would include head coach Stephanie White , whom they believe has not found the right way to get the most out of Clark, Aliyah Boston and Kelsey Mitchell together.

Indiana has confirmed that president of basketball and business operations Kelly Krauskopf is stepping down and that general manager and COO Amber Cox has left the organization. The team plans to conduct a national search for its next GM, but has not announced a replacement.

Caitlin Clark had nothing but gratitude for Stephanie White

White, meanwhile, is expected to remain Indiana’s head coach , according to ESPN sources, though the Fever has not officially confirmed the report. Her coaching has drawn criticism from fans who feel Clark is sometimes underused or pushed into the background.

But Clark herself spoke warmly about White after the season, saying, “I really appreciate Steph.” She also praised the time and effort the coaching staff put into helping the team succeed and said she was grateful for them.

That response doesn’t mean Clark publicly campaigned for White to return. It does show that the relationship may look different from the outside than it does inside the team.

Clark also acknowledged that when a season falls short of expectations, responsibility belongs to the players as well as the coaching staff. Reese’s move to Atlanta wasn’t a guaranteed ticket to the Finals. She arrived in a trade without knowing how the season would unfold, and the Dream hadn’t reached the championship series since 2013, a 13-year wait.

Now, after Atlanta’s 67-62 loss in Game 4, the series is tied 2-2, and Reese has admitted she rushed her shots and didn’t give herself enough time to finish around the basket. Her path is remarkable, but it’s no promise that changing teams will lead to a title.

articles.title: The harshest criticism of Angel Reese: “Just embarrassed herself on the biggest stage”
articles.standfirst: The Atlanta Dream and Angel Reese suffered a tough blow this Saturday, October 24.
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream and Angel Reese suffered a tough blow this Saturday, October 24.
articles.body:
After two standout performances that had kept the team in contention for the WNBA title, Game 4 of the Finals ended very differently for Atlanta’s star, who struggled to find her rhythm on the court.

The Golden State Valkyries secured a 67-62 victory , tied the series, and put Reese at the center of criticism over her offensive struggles.

Angel Reese had a difficult afternoon

Reese finished the game with just eight points and nine rebounds after making only two of her 12 field-goal attempts, shooting 16.7% . Her struggles to find the basket made a significant difference in a game where every score could have brought Atlanta closer to victory.

Foul trouble and turnovers added to her difficulties, further complicating her performance. Although the loss reflected the Dream’s overall performance, Reese’s individual numbers drew particular attention given the contrast with her previous outings.

Atlanta had an opportunity to take the series lead and move closer to the championship, but ultimately fell to a Valkyries team that took advantage of the result to even things up.

Yahoo delivers harsh criticism of Angel Reese

The Atlanta star’s performance did not go unnoticed by journalist Landon Kardian , who published an article on Yahoo with a blunt headline: “Angel Reese Just Embarrassed Herself on the Biggest Stage,” a phrase that sharply questions her performance in the game.

The criticism focused on her offensive struggles and inability to consistently convert the opportunities she had near the basket.

Following this difficult performance, the championship could be decided on Monday, October 26 , when the two teams meet at Chase Center in San Francisco.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark reclaims her place in the WNBA while Angel Reese takes a step back in the WNBA Finals
articles.standfirst: Clark returns to the WNBA’s elite ranks, while Reese and the Atlanta Dream face renewed pressure after their Finals setback
articles.summary: Clark returns to the WNBA’s elite ranks, while Reese and the Atlanta Dream face renewed pressure after their Finals setback
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark has returned to WNBA’s elite company, earning a place on the 2026 All-WNBA First Team, while Angel Reese faces the challenge of rediscovering her scoring touch as the championship series intensifies.

Clark’s selection recognizes another impressive season with the Indiana Fever, where her scoring ability and playmaking have established her among the league’s most influential guards.

She averaged 22.5 points and 8.4 assists per game, ranking third in scoring and tying for the league lead in assists.

The honor marks Clark’s second first-team selection after earning the distinction as a rookie in 2024. She joins teammate Kelsey Mitchell , who averaged 24.7 points per game, on a Fever backcourt that delivered exceptional offensive production throughout the regular season.

Las Vegas Aces star A’ja Wilson , New York Liberty forward Breanna Stewart and Minnesota Lynx guard Olivia Miles complete the first team. Wilson followed another MVP-winning campaign with her sixth first-team selection, while Miles enjoyed an outstanding rookie season that earned her recognition among the league’s best players.

Despite their individual achievements, none of the first-team selections feature in the 2026 WNBA Finals between the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries.

Angel Reese faces a response test as Finals pressure builds

While Clark celebrates her individual recognition, Reese is preparing for a crucial response after Atlanta’s momentum was interrupted in Game 4 of the WNBA Finals.

The Dream suffered a 67-62 defeat against the Valkyries on Saturday missing an opportunity to move within one victory of the championship. The result levelled the best-of-seven series at 2-2, increasing the pressure on both teams heading into the decisive stretch.

Reese , who was named the 2026 Defensive Player of the Year and earned a place on the All-WNBA Second Team, finished with eight points, nine rebounds, three assists, one steal and three blocks.

Her offensive struggles were particularly noticeable after two outstanding performances in the previous games. Reese recorded 30 points and 16 rebounds in Game 2 before producing 21 points and 12 rebounds in Game 3. Against Golden State, however, she struggled to find her rhythm around the basket.

“I think I rushed a lot of my shots and I didn’t take my time and finish around the basket like I’ve been doing in the last 3 games,” Reese said after the defeat. She acknowledged the problem and emphasized her determination to improve in the next game.

Atlanta still has an opportunity to regain control of the series. Rhyne Howard led the Dream with 19 points and eight rebounds, while Jordin Canada and Isobel Borlase contributed 10 points apiece. Howard also earned second-team All-WNBA honors alongside Reese .

The Valkyries will now look to maintain their defensive intensity in Game 5 on Monday, October 26, at Chase Center.

articles.title: The two teams that could separate Sophie Cunningham from Caitlin Clark and give her the contract she wants
articles.standfirst: The 30-year-old guard will become an unrestricted free agent after completing a one-season contract with Indiana. Two teams are among the possible destinations, although for now there is no official confirmation of negotiations, and Cunningham has already made it clear that she is seeking stability and a multi-year deal.
articles.summary: The 30-year-old guard will become an unrestricted free agent after completing a one-season contract with Indiana. Two teams are among the possible destinations, although for now there is no official confirmation of negotiations, and Cunningham has already made it clear that she is seeking stability and a multi-year deal.
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham will be one of the names to watch in the upcoming WNBA free agency. Portland Fire and Los Angeles Sparks have been mentioned as possible teams interested in the veteran shooting guard, although for now there is no official confirmation of contacts or negotiations. Indiana Fever, meanwhile, continues to appear as the main option to retain her, with the length of the next contract being one of the decisive factors.

Cunningham finished the 2026 season averaging 7.9 points, 2.3 rebounds and 1.2 assists per game in 43 appearances. She also made 41.9% of her three-pointers and was Indiana’s leading scorer off the bench, numbers that maintain her value within a team built around Caitlin Clark, Aliyah Boston and Kelsey Mitchell.

A multi-year contract, the key condition

The length of the agreement is no minor detail for Cunningham. In April, she signed for one season with the Fever, on a reported $665,000 contract , and later clarified that her dissatisfaction was not related to the salary. “I just wanted more years because I love being here”, she explained at the time, noting that she was looking to establish herself permanently in Indiana.

The player also confirmed that she had received multi-year offers from other teams before deciding to remain with the Fever in 2026. At that time, Cunningham prioritized staying with a group where she felt comfortable, even though other destinations offered the contractual security she was looking for.

Indiana expressed interest in keeping her after the playoff elimination. Amber Cox, then the franchise's general manager, highlighted her leadership, experience, and ability to connect the locker room, in addition to her two seasons of strong perimeter play. However, Cox left her position on October 23, and the Fever began a nationwide search to find her replacement, a change that adds another variable to the team's decisions for 2027.

Portland and Los Angeles now appear among the possible alternatives for Cunningham, but it is still a market scenario . So far, there is no announced agreement or public confirmation that either of the two teams has initiated formal talks with the player.

Cunningham arrived in Indiana from Phoenix before the 2025 season and remained with the Fever for two campaigns. After recovering from the medial collateral ligament injury that prematurely ended her 2025 season, she returned in 2026 and once again established herself as one of the second unit’s main perimeter threats.

For now, there is no new contract announced .

Cunningham will be able to assess the market as an unrestricted free agent and, if Indiana intends to keep her alongside Clark and the rest of its core, the length of the offer appears to be one of the central points of the negotiation.

Portland Fire and Los Angeles Sparks appear as possibilities, but their interest will have to be confirmed when free agency begins to formally move.

articles.title: Crisis Solved: WNBA reaches agreement with Hawks over Game 6 arena clash
articles.standfirst: The Dream will retain their home-court advantage at State Farm Arena after negotiations produce a rare NBA and WNBA doubleheader
articles.summary: The Dream will retain their home-court advantage at State Farm Arena after negotiations produce a rare NBA and WNBA doubleheader
articles.body:
A championship game deserves a championship atmosphere, and the WNBA has secured precisely that for Game 6 of the Finals. Whether supporters can actually attend at the newly announced time, however, is another matter.

The league confirmed Monday that the Atlanta Dream will host the Golden State Valkyries at State Farm Arena on October 29, avoiding the possibility of moving one of the season's biggest games to a considerably smaller venue.

The agreement required cooperation from the Atlanta Hawks , who share the arena and were already scheduled to face the Cleveland Cavaliers that evening.

Instead of relocating either game, the organizations agreed to an unusual doubleheader. The WNBA Finals will begin at 12:30 p.m. ET, followed by the Hawks ' NBA matchup at 8 p.m.

While the compromise resolves the venue dispute, it leaves fans facing an inconvenient weekday tip-off.

The alternative would have been particularly disappointing for Atlanta, which has enjoyed tremendous support throughout its postseason run.

State Farm Arena accommodates approximately 17,000 spectators, compared with just 3,500 at Gateway Center Arena , the Dream's usual home venue.

Games 3 and 4 of the Finals attracted sellout crowds at State Farm Arena, demonstrating the demand for women's basketball in Atlanta.

WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert welcomed the agreement, emphasizing the importance of keeping the championship series at the larger venue.

"The sellout crowds and extraordinary atmosphere at State Farm Arena for Games 3 and 4 were a tremendous success, and we're excited to give thousands more fans the opportunity to experience Game 6 with a championship on the line," Engelbert said.

However, supporters hoping to attend must now reorganize their schedules, with the new start time creating obvious difficulties for people working or attending school.

Scheduling conflict forces unusual compromise

The Hawks ' existing commitments made finding an alternative date particularly difficult.

Atlanta faces the Miami Heat on Wednesday evening, leaving insufficient recovery time for the team to accommodate an early Thursday NBA game.

Moving the Hawks ' meeting with Cleveland to Friday would also complicate the Cavaliers ' schedule before their Saturday matchup against the Milwaukee Bucks .

Meanwhile, postponing Game 6 would have threatened the timing of a potential Game 7 in San Francisco, where the Golden State Warriors have upcoming home commitments.

The agreement avoids those complications and preserves the WNBA's existing championship schedule.

Atlanta Dream prepare for crucial Finals showdown

The series remains tied at 2-2 heading into Monday's Game 5 in California, meaning Thursday's contest could determine the championship.

Dream guard Jordin Canada welcomed the opportunity to return to State Farm Arena despite the unusual timing.

"The crowd has showed up and showed out for Games 3 and 4 so looking forward to being at State Farm for Game 6," Canada told reporters.

Thursday's game will be televised on USA Network and streamed through Peacock, with the league planning additional promotional efforts to raise awareness of the change.

A potential Game 7 remains scheduled for Saturday, October 31, at Chase Center in San Francisco.

The WNBA has protected the atmosphere surrounding its championship series, but the midday tip-off remains an awkward price for securing Atlanta's preferred venue.

articles.title: Angel Reese accused of playing dirty during Game 5 of the WNBA Finals
articles.standfirst: The Golden State Valkyries are one win away from history after Kiah Stokes delivered a Finals masterpiece and pushed Atlanta Dream to the brink of elimination.
articles.summary: The Golden State Valkyries are one win away from history after Kiah Stokes delivered a Finals masterpiece and pushed Atlanta Dream to the brink of elimination.
articles.body:
A ngel Reese is, without a doubt, the player attracting the most attention in the WNBA Finals . But this time she has become the center of attention for fans because of her physical play, which many believe has crossed the line.

The Atlanta Dream forward is being accused of using her elbows in a violent manner against Golden State Valkyries players, particularly for the actions observed during the first quarter of Game 5 of the series.

Tough defeat for the Atlanta Dream and Angel Reese

Kiah Stokes delivered a huge performance with 13 points, eight rebounds and three blocks as the Golden State Valkyries moved one win away from their first WNBA championship, defeating the Atlanta Dream 64-55 in Game 5 of the Finals on Monday night.

The second-year expansion franchise now leads the series 3-2 and can clinch the title with a victory in Game 6 on Thursday in Atlanta .

While Angel Reese posted another strong rebounding night with 15 boards, five assists and seven points, she couldn’t replicate the dominant performances that helped Atlanta win the first two games of the series at Chase Center.

Stokes became the unlikely hero for Golden State on a night when leading scorer Gabby Williams struggled offensively. Williams finished with just nine points on 3-of-14 shooting, but the Valkyries once again showed the depth behind coach Natalie Nakase’s “strength in numbers” philosophy .

Veronica Burton matched Stokes with 13 points and eight rebounds, while veteran Tiffany Hayes added 12 points after earning another start following a lineup change that helped Golden State win Game 4.

The Valkyries entered halftime with a slim 25-22 lead, marking the lowest-scoring first half in WNBA Finals history. Neither team found rhythm from beyond the arc, combining to shoot just 5-of-29 from three-point range.

But Golden State took control in the second half, making the biggest plays when it mattered most. Stokes hit two crucial three-pointers, including one late in the third quarter and another with 7:21 remaining, sending the Chase Center crowd into a frenzy with chants of “Ki-ah! Ki-ah!”

The center also made history by recording three or more blocks in six consecutive playoff games, tying Lisa Leslie’s 2003 WNBA postseason record for the longest streak of its kind.

Atlanta struggled to keep pace, committing 17 turnovers that turned into 21 Golden State points. Despite a late push led by Rhyne Howard , the Dream couldn’t overcome the Valkyries’ defensive intensity and clutch execution.

Now, Atlanta faces elimination on Thursday in Game 6 at State Farm Arena, where the Dream must win to force a decisive Game 7 back at Chase Center on Saturday.

Golden State’s rapid rise has already exceeded expectations. When owner Joe Lacob secured the expansion franchise, he predicted a championship within five years. The Valkyries now stand just one victory away from making that bold promise a reality in only their second season.
